docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:4365:| Venue fit | **3** | Self-assessment is commendably honest in tone, but contradicts the project's own venue table: CSCSU's 5-pages-including-references budget makes the "§§2–6 reused nearly intact" plan physically impossible, no workshop is named (EuroMLSys/HotCarbon are already identified in-repo), the invented ICPE-full criteria do not match the roadmap's, and the dual-submission collision with the MVP paper is never mentioned. |
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:4393:The proposal states it "reuses the MVP draft's Sections 2–6 nearly intact" and consumes the identical D-117 dataset. Relative to the MVP paper it therefore has **no new measurements, no new method, and no new data** — only a new output format for the same numbers. Two papers sharing §§2–6 near-verbatim and one dataset, submitted to a capstone and then ICPE, is a live ACM prior/concurrent-publication problem. The proposal never names the risk, never proposes a partition of contributions, and its "what is new" list (schema, comparability rules, mutation evaluation, audit) is exactly the list F1 just dissolved.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:4432:3. **Papadopoulos et al., "Methodological Principles for Reproducible Performance Evaluation in Cloud Computing"** (SPEC-RG-2019-04 / IEEE TSE 2021, ICSE 2020 Journal-First) — eight principles, a decision procedure, and an audit of an existing benchmark against them, from **SPEC's own research group**. The exact structural analogue of this entire proposal. Cite it or be caught. (Adjacent: Raasveldt et al., "Fair Benchmarking Considered Difficult", DBTEST@SIGMOD 2018 — a pitfalls-and-detection paper with no new system.)
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:4480:`docs/strategy/2026-08-06-impressiveness-roadmap.md` §"Venue ambition" already fixes the ladder with cited page limits:
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:4482:- **CSCSU: 5 pages *including references*.** The proposal's core mechanism — "reuses the MVP draft's Sections 2–6 nearly intact" — cannot be executed twice inside 5-page budgets. At the capstone venue there is room for one paper, and §§2–6 are already spoken for. The reuse plan is not merely redundant; it does not fit.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:4484:- **ICPE full track**: the roadmap enumerates the qualifying deeper contributions — "held-out Q4 prediction, second-unit replication, or a successful mechanism study" — on top of C1–C8, cross-day stability, and artifact-ready release, at 28% acceptance. **A reporting label is not on that list.** The proposal invents its own ICPE-full criteria ("executable validator, reporting audit, artifact-quality release, and preferably external adoption") and then gates on external adoption, which is unreachable in a capstone timeline and is in any case fenced by C5-3.5.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:4485:- Roadmap **rank 3, "Artifact-evaluation-quality release" (4–6 weeks, 0 measurement nights)**, already covers the validator/renderer/reproducible-provenance work, and ICPE runs a dedicated artifact-evaluation track aligned to it. The proposal re-derives a large part of rank 3 as a novel paper contribution without citing it.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:4487:**Partial correction in the proposal's favour, which it did not claim for itself.** On the charge's question (a) — *can a standards paper without new measurements carry weight at the target venue?* — the answer is **yes, but only in the right track**. ICPE's **Emerging Research track** explicitly solicits "new ideas and vision papers on emerging research challenges" and states that some aspects may "remain open, possibly with limited or no evaluation" (it was formerly the Work-in-Progress and Vision track). **HotCarbon** explicitly solicits "research **and position** papers"; **LOCO** welcomes "new ideas and visions." So the genre is admissible — at Emerging/WIP and workshop tier, which is exactly where the roadmap already placed it and where the proposal declined to look. Two caveats: the **ICPE 2026 cycle has closed** (4–8 May 2026, Florence; research abstracts were due 3 Nov 2025), so the real target is ICPE 2027; and the sweep **could not find a single named ICPE paper that is purely a reporting standard with zero new measurements** — permitted by track scope, but unevidenced by precedent. Do not let that be asserted unsupported.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:4503:**2b. Pick the venue the project already picked, and the track the genre actually fits.** Target **HotCarbon** (5 pp excl. refs; explicitly solicits position papers; explicitly wants a stronger sustainability-metrics argument — a refusal calculus for energy comparisons is exactly that) or **EuroMLSys** (6 pp). For ICPE, target the **Emerging Research track at ICPE 2027** — it takes vision papers with limited or no evaluation by construction; the 2026 cycle is closed and the full research track's qualifying deeper contributions (held-out Q4 prediction, second-unit replication, mechanism study) do not include this. Send the validator to **ICPE's artifact-evaluation track** as roadmap rank 3, not as a research-paper contribution. Verify ICPE 2027 page limits directly — the sweep could not confirm them.

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:9988:**Thesis:** An Apple software power counter can support reproducible, phase-resolved LLM energy research only when in-session calibration determines both what it can measure and what it must refuse; full characterization, held-out workload prediction, and wall-boundary validation elevate JouleWise from a capstone demonstration to an ICPE-quality metrology paper.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:9994:The ICPE delta should then be disciplined rather than broad: collect the already-designed metrology suite in two or three windows; run the promoted Q4 4×3 workload-shape study in two or three windows; borrow Suzanne Rivoire’s lab WT310E for a pilot and confirmatory whole-machine validation; and package a hardware-free raw-to-figure artifact. Total target: **9–10 claim sessions**, comprising D-117’s three plus **6–7 additional sessions**, with one contingency night reserved but not silently used for outcome-dependent top-up.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:10018:Owned: M3 Max/128 GB, pinned MLX/Qwen artifacts, `powermetrics`, and existing calibration/custody machinery. The RTX 3080 Ti and Jetsons are unnecessary. Borrowed: an in-calibration Yokogawa WT310E, safe inline fixture, and its export interface. **Wall-meter dependency: yes for this proposed ICPE-full version**, but no for the underlying MVP. If a qualified loan and safe fixture cannot be secured, do not substitute a consumer plug; submit the metrology core to a workshop or ICPE Emerging track.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:10022:This is a strong capstone chapter immediately after D-117. ICPE full-track fit comes from the combination of instrument characterization, falsifiable held-out performance prediction, physical-boundary validation, and an artifact reviewers can replay. It reuses the MVP draft’s introduction, related-work gap, measurement model, pulse calibration, floor composition, fail-closed protocol, custody rules, and single-stack limitations. New material is the completed C1–C8 results, cross-day stability, Q4 prediction study, wall regression, and artifact evaluation. Without Q4 or equivalent depth, the work remains an excellent metrology workshop paper rather than a convincing full research-track submission.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:10026:Kill the ICPE upgrade before spending expansion nights if D-117 cannot mint valid floors; the 150-config metrology suite cannot be repacked below four hours with 20% margin; fresh ramp diagnostics cannot safely place micro-deltas around the operative floor; or Q4 dry runs show missing phases, capped contexts, or a campaign budget above three nights. Kill wall validation if the meter lacks current calibration, safe fixture, adequate synchronized sampling, fixed-range uncertainty at Mac loads, or battery-charge neutralization. A failed Q4 holdout or load-dependent wall discrepancy does not kill the paper—both are publishable findings—but they prohibit predictive or simple-gain claims.

Kill wall validation if the meter lacks current calibration, safe fixture, adequate synchronized sampling, fixed-range uncertainty at Mac loads, or battery-charge neutralization. A failed Q4 holdout or load-dependent wall discrepancy does not kill the paper—both are publishable findings—but they prohibit predictive or simple-gain claims.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:10745:**Thesis:** An Apple software power counter can support reproducible, phase-resolved LLM energy research only when in-session calibration determines both what it can measure and what it must refuse; full characterization, held-out workload prediction, and wall-boundary validation elevate JouleWise from a capstone demonstration to an ICPE-quality metrology paper.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:10751:The ICPE delta should then be disciplined rather than broad: collect the already-designed metrology suite in two or three windows; run the promoted Q4 4×3 workload-shape study in two or three windows; borrow Suzanne Rivoire’s lab WT310E for a pilot and confirmatory whole-machine validation; and package a hardware-free raw-to-figure artifact. Total target: **9–10 claim sessions**, comprising D-117’s three plus **6–7 additional sessions**, with one contingency night reserved but not silently used for outcome-dependent top-up.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:10775:Owned: M3 Max/128 GB, pinned MLX/Qwen artifacts, `powermetrics`, and existing calibration/custody machinery. The RTX 3080 Ti and Jetsons are unnecessary. Borrowed: an in-calibration Yokogawa WT310E, safe inline fixture, and its export interface. **Wall-meter dependency: yes for this proposed ICPE-full version**, but no for the underlying MVP. If a qualified loan and safe fixture cannot be secured, do not substitute a consumer plug; submit the metrology core to a workshop or ICPE Emerging track.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:10779:This is a strong capstone chapter immediately after D-117. ICPE full-track fit comes from the combination of instrument characterization, falsifiable held-out performance prediction, physical-boundary validation, and an artifact reviewers can replay. It reuses the MVP draft’s introduction, related-work gap, measurement model, pulse calibration, floor composition, fail-closed protocol, custody rules, and single-stack limitations. New material is the completed C1–C8 results, cross-day stability, Q4 prediction study, wall regression, and artifact evaluation. Without Q4 or equivalent depth, the work remains an excellent metrology workshop paper rather than a convincing full research-track submission.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:10783:Kill the ICPE upgrade before spending expansion nights if D-117 cannot mint valid floors; the 150-config metrology suite cannot be repacked below four hours with 20% margin; fresh ramp diagnostics cannot safely place micro-deltas around the operative floor; or Q4 dry runs show missing phases, capped contexts, or a campaign budget above three nights. docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:10803:rev-mvp-icpe-upgrade.md	**VERDICT: WEAK** — sound core, fatal flaw in the thing that makes it an *upgrade*. 
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:10946:The MVP is fixed and remains the highest-value use of every immediate desk hour. Its scientific spine is already distinctive: phase attribution is systematically limited, repetitions do not remove that limit, and the instrument publishes what it cannot resolve. Honest cost is **four nights**—3.14 h alpha, 3.24 h beta, 2.80 h gamma, and one 2–4 h Window-C characterization night—plus roughly **2–4 concentrated desk/review weeks** for the open D-117 machinery and postcollection pin closure. I estimate an **80–90% chance that a defensible paper survives**, but only about **55–65% that every desired claim cell and characterization row passes without a refusal**. That distinction is healthy: valid refusals still support the paper. The MVP-review verdict was WEAK only as an overgrown ICPE upgrade, not as the capstone paper itself.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:10974:The desk-only tokenizer proposal is not a paper, but one added matched-content, non-Latin measurement night could make it one. Compare deployable Qwen and OLMo-family stacks on the same semantic content budgeted by characters/bytes, report gross J/request first, and ask whether J/token reverses the ranking. The effect should be large, but the claim must remain “reporting distortion between as-shipped stacks,” not causal tokenizer attribution, because architecture and precision also differ. Cost is **five nights total**, **1–3 desk weeks**, and one claim window with its own floors. Survival prior: **40–55%** for an actual flip. Venue ceiling is workshop/tool-track rather than ICPE full, but it cleanly serves Ed’s reporting goal.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:10993:- **wall-meter-validation — KILL as a standalone paper.** Keep C8 as a conditional MVP/ICPE subsection after battery, fan, fixture, loan, and identifiability gates pass.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/SYNTHESIS-IMPACT-FIRST.md:11022:After the MVP’s tables and artifact are locked, spend 4–6 weeks on the MoE gates. If all pass, collect one floor night and one mechanism night; add a third only if that need is determined prospectively by the frozen floor design. Target EuroMLSys or ICPE Emerging first; upgrade venue ambition only if the dense comparison, routing intervention, and replay artifact all land.

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-mtp-energy.md:1775:| **ICPE Emerging/WIP** | Appropriate if the core is strong but external validation, replication, or the broader predictive evaluation remains incomplete. docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-mtp-energy.md:1776:| **ICPE full research track** | Plausible over months, but not yet supported by the current evidence. The 2026 research track used 10 pages and judged novelty, technical quality, and scientific soundness; 2026’s reported full-paper acceptance rate was 28%. [ICPE 2027](https://icpe2027.spec.org/tracks-and-submissions/research-paper-track/), [2026 research criteria](https://icpe2026.spec.org/tracks-and-submissions/research-paper-track/), [acceptance history](https://icpe.spec.org/past-conferences/) | C1–C8, cross-day stability, artifact-ready release, and at least one deeper contribution: held-out Q4 prediction, second-unit replication, or a successful mechanism study. Split is not required. |

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-mtp-energy.md:6662:A passed, well-resolved MTP result materially strengthens an ICPE full-paper case because it demonstrates that the instrument answers a real systems-mechanism question. An unresolved or energy-negative result still fits EuroMLSys/ICPE Emerging or a strong capstone paper, provided the refusal is treated as a result rather than hidden.

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-open-explore-contrarian.md:1836:| **CSCSU** | After remint and clean C/D, this should be a strong undergraduate-conference submission. The latest published rules allow technical papers and extensive experimentation, with **5 pages including references**. docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-open-explore-contrarian.md:1838:| **ICPE Emerging/WIP** | Appropriate if the core is strong but external validation, replication, or the broader predictive evaluation remains incomplete. The 2026 track used a 6-page format. docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-open-explore-contrarian.md:1839:| **ICPE full research track** | Plausible over months, but not yet supported by the current evidence. ICPE 2027 lists research and artifact tracks but their details and dates remain TBA. The 2026 research track used 10 pages and judged novelty, technical quality, and scientific soundness; 2026’s reported full-paper acceptance rate was 28%. [ICPE 2027](https://icpe2027.spec.org/tracks-and-submissions/research-paper-track/), [2026 research criteria](https://icpe2026.spec.org/tracks-and-submissions/research-paper-track/), [acceptance history](https://icpe.spec.org/past-conferences/) | C1–C8, cross-day stability, artifact-ready release, and at least one deeper contribution: held-out Q4 prediction, second-unit replication, or a successful mechanism study. Split is not required. |

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-open-explore-contrarian.md:5565:docs/run_reports/2026-07-30-sweep-cv-paths.md:27:- **HotCarbon** (co-located w/ major systems conf, papers published archivally in ACM SIGEnergy Energy Informatics Review): 5-page limit, double-blind, explicitly favors papers that "stimulate reflection and discussion" and open lines of inquiry — position papers welcome ([CFP](https://hotcarbon.org/cfp)). The [2025 accepted list](https://hotcarbon.org/2025) (19 papers) includes directly comparable scope and team shapes: *"Energy Efficient or Exhaustive? Benchmarking Power Consumption of LLM Inference Engines"* (4 authors, Texas Tech + LBNL) and *"LLMCO2: Carbon Footprint Prediction for LLM Inferences"* (5 authors, Indiana + Purdue). Small university teams are the norm, not the exception. Acceptance rate is unpublished (flagged: hot-topics workshops of this kind typically land roughly 40–60% — that's a guess). **HotCarbon '26 already happened (July 16–17, 2026; deadline was May 18)** — the target is HotCarbon '27, deadline ~May 2027 (guess from pattern; not yet announced).

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-energy-nutrition-label.md:681:| **CSCSU** | After remint and clean C/D, this should be a strong undergraduate-conference submission. The 2026 track used a 6-page format. docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-energy-nutrition-label.md:684:| **ICPE full research track** | Plausible over months, but not yet supported by the current evidence. [ICPE 2027](https://icpe2027.spec.org/tracks-and-submissions/research-paper-track/), [2026 research criteria](https://icpe2026.spec.org/tracks-and-submissions/research-paper-track/), [acceptance history](https://icpe.spec.org/past-conferences/) | C1–C8, cross-day stability, artifact-ready release, and at least one deeper contribution: held-out Q4 prediction, second-unit replication, or a successful mechanism study. Split is not required. |

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-energy-nutrition-label.md:4291:docs/run_reports/2026-07-30-sweep-cv-paths.md:85:**Ship the tool + blog post first (fall 2026), submit the workshop paper second (winter/spring 2027), convert repro discipline into an ICPE artifact badge if the dates cooperate.** These three compound: the tool release makes the workshop paper *stronger* (reviewers can install what the paper describes — rare and disarming), the paper makes the tool *credible* (the validation story becomes citable), and the badge or well-documented repo covers whichever audience the other two miss. The niche is verifiably open — the only existing Apple Silicon ML-energy library has 8 stars and a README disclaiming its own accuracy — and the exact skillset appears verbatim in current NVIDIA and Apple new-grad/perf-power postings, which is the strongest industry-side evidence found. Skip the live leaderboard (funded-lab economics, solo-maintenance trap) in favor of a dated static results page; skip CCGrid (wrong audience, highest bar, earliest deadline). One deliberate gap to accept: nothing lands as "published" before Dec 2026 grad deadlines, so if Fall 2027 PhD entry matters, the EuroMLSys/ICPE submission should be timed to be "under review" by application season — otherwise the calendar is comfortable.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-energy-nutrition-label.md:4625:Base paper cost is exactly the three D-117 windows. A fourth, independently calibrated 256-token prefill window is optional for an ICPE-strengthened version only; it needs matching floor cells or a preregistered transport rule and likely about 110 core minutes plus bookends. No extension may be appended to gamma after freeze. Required new harness work is label serialization, completeness/comparability validation, and artifact-to-label rendering. It does not alter the frozen sequential, single-request boundary.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-energy-nutrition-label.md:4633:This is an excellent capstone/CSCSU chapter and a credible performance- or sustainable-systems workshop paper. ICPE full-track fit is plausible only with the executable validator, the reporting audit, artifact-quality release, and preferably external adoption or wall-boundary extension; the label idea alone is too modest.

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-spec-decode-energy.md:6070:./docs/run_reports/2026-07-30-sweep-cv-paths.md:27:- **HotCarbon** (co-located w/ major systems conf, papers published archivally in ACM SIGEnergy Energy Informatics Review): 5-page limit, double-blind, explicitly favors papers that "stimulate reflection and discussion" and open lines of inquiry — position papers welcome ([CFP](https://hotcarbon.org/cfp)). The [2025 accepted list](https://hotcarbon.org/2025) (19 papers) includes directly comparable scope and team shapes: *"Energy Efficient or Exhaustive? Benchmarking Power Consumption of LLM Inference Engines"* (4 authors, Texas Tech + LBNL) and *"LLMCO2: Carbon Footprint Prediction for LLM Inferences"* (5 authors, Indiana + Purdue). Small university teams are the norm, not the exception. Acceptance rate is unpublished (flagged: hot-topics workshops of this kind typically land roughly 40–60% — that's a guess). **HotCarbon '26 already happened (July 16–17, 2026; deadline was May 18)** — the target is HotCarbon '27, deadline ~May 2027 (guess from pattern; not yet announced).
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-spec-decode-energy.md:7628:For ICPE full research, the mechanism result supplies the deeper systems contribution the MVP alone lacks. EuroMLSys or an ICPE emerging/WIP track remains appropriate if the break-even interval is broad or the result is chiefly a well-supported refusal. The claim cannot be “first speculative-decoding energy study”; its novelty is calibrated, floor-gated evidence on named consumer silicon.

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-mvp-icpe-upgrade.md:4545:**Thesis:** An Apple software power counter can support reproducible, phase-resolved LLM energy research only when in-session calibration determines both what it can measure and what it must refuse; full characterization, held-out workload prediction, and wall-boundary validation elevate JouleWise from a capstone demonstration to an ICPE-quality metrology paper.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-mvp-icpe-upgrade.md:4551:The ICPE delta should then be disciplined rather than broad: collect the already-designed metrology suite in two or three windows; run the promoted Q4 4×3 workload-shape study in two or three windows; borrow Suzanne Rivoire’s lab WT310E for a pilot and confirmatory whole-machine validation; and package a hardware-free raw-to-figure artifact. Total target: **9–10 claim sessions**, comprising D-117’s three plus **6–7 additional sessions**, with one contingency night reserved but not silently used for outcome-dependent top-up.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-mvp-icpe-upgrade.md:4575:Owned: M3 Max/128 GB, pinned MLX/Qwen artifacts, `powermetrics`, and existing calibration/custody machinery. The RTX 3080 Ti and Jetsons are unnecessary. Borrowed: an in-calibration Yokogawa WT310E, safe inline fixture, and its export interface. **Wall-meter dependency: yes for this proposed ICPE-full version**, but no for the underlying MVP. If a qualified loan and safe fixture cannot be secured, do not substitute a consumer plug; submit the metrology core to a workshop or ICPE Emerging track.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-mvp-icpe-upgrade.md:4579:This is a strong capstone chapter immediately after D-117. ICPE full-track fit comes from the combination of instrument characterization, falsifiable held-out performance prediction, physical-boundary validation, and an artifact reviewers can replay. It reuses the MVP draft’s introduction, related-work gap, measurement model, pulse calibration, floor composition, fail-closed protocol, custody rules, and single-stack limitations. New material is the completed C1–C8 results, cross-day stability, Q4 prediction study, wall regression, and artifact evaluation. Without Q4 or equivalent depth, the work remains an excellent metrology workshop paper rather than a convincing full research-track submission.
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-mvp-icpe-upgrade.md:4583:Kill the ICPE upgrade before spending expansion nights if D-117 cannot mint valid floors; the 150-config metrology suite cannot be repacked below four hours with 20% margin; fresh ramp diagnostics cannot safely place micro-deltas around the operative floor; or Q4 dry runs show missing phases, capped contexts, or a campaign budget above three nights. Kill wall validation if the meter lacks current calibration, safe fixture, adequate synchronized sampling, fixed-range uncertainty at Mac loads, or battery-charge neutralization. A failed Q4 holdout or load-dependent wall discrepancy does not kill the paper—both are publishable findings—but they prohibit predictive or simple-gain claims.

# Capstone report source (RPT-001 vertical slice + RPT-002 literature)

Canonical report source per `docs/specs/c027/rpt-001_report_vertical_slice.md`:
Pandoc-compatible Markdown, assembled by a stdlib-only script into one
deterministic Markdown document. No LaTeX/Pandoc/PDF engine is part of the
build gate; the final renderer is a P1-008 decision behind the
`format_adapter` seam in `report.json`.

## Layout

- `report.json` — report profile: ordered chapter manifest + format-adapter seam.
- `references.csl.json` — canonical offline CSL bibliography.
- `source_map.json` — seven-source RPT-002 evidence/verification map; all
  intake records were `VERIFIED_AGAINST_PRIMARY` by the lead on 2026-07-11.
- `chapters/`, `appendices/` — authored prose (edit these).
- `generated/` — build outputs inside the source tree (do NOT edit; first
  line carries a GENERATED marker).
- `report.md` — human-readable pointer to the manifest.

## Build / regeneration

Source-only assembly and `--check` are reproducible from a pristine clone:

```sh
python3 scripts/build_capstone.py --profile rpt001 --offline --check
```

This path uses only tracked analysis and report sources. It compares the
committed generated page, validates full-report assembly in memory, and exits
2 on drift. It neither requires `runs/` nor uses the untracked assembled
document as a reference.

Full evidence re-derivation is **controlled/internal**, not a clean-clone or
external reproducibility claim. The following command re-derives the dataset,
aggregates, figure F1, tables T1/S1, claims-index row, generated results page,
and assembled report only when the internal corpus is available:

```sh
python3 scripts/build_capstone.py --profile rpt001 --full --offline \
  --runs-root runs
```

It requires controlled access to the six pinned legacy bundles under `runs/`
(internal, ~110 MB, gitignored). Neither the pristine clone nor the
privacy-transformed public projection supplies strict-valid, independently
re-reducible replacements for that corpus. The assembled document lands at
`build/capstone/rpt001/report.md` (untracked). If the controlled corpus lives
elsewhere, pass that path to `--runs-root`; committed artifacts always store
repo-relative paths.

To re-pin input hashes after an intentional corpus change (this is a
versioning event — see the spec's rpt001-v2 rule):

```sh
python3 scripts/make_figures.py --runs-root runs \
  --bootstrap-input-manifest
```

## Evidence boundary

All current results content is **legacy L1 (manual review; pre-2M)**:
stack-specific instrument observations from six legacy bundles, n=3 per
exact stack. No cross-stack comparison, efficiency ranking, or scaling claim
is made anywhere in this source tree, and the assembler fails the build on a
small forbidden-phrase list.

## Bibliography verification boundary

The original eleven-source survey inherits its 2026-07-06 verification record
from `docs/phase_4/related_work_draft.md`. The lead verified all seven RPT-002
sources against primary records on 2026-07-11. `references.csl.json` contains
the corrected metadata; each source-map entry records the verified primary
URLs, retrieval date, scope boundary, claim wording, artifact status, and
completed primary-paper checks.

The assembler parses both JSON files, validates their structure, checks all
Pandoc citation keys offline, and requires the seven intake records to retain
an explicit recognized verification state.

## Known gaps vs the full RPT-001 spec (vertical slice, time-boxed)

- `{{jw:include-section}}` contract transclusion: not implemented; the
  assembler supports whole-file `{{jw:include path="..."}}` only. Chapters
  reference contracts instead of mirroring exact wording.
- `claims_lint --mode phase4` and the generated
  `docs/phase_4/claims_index.md` view: not yet implemented.
- Offline (`--offline`) CI build mode and the CI hook: not yet wired.
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""RPT-001/RPT-002 capstone report assembler (stdlib only).

Reads the report profile ``docs/report_src/report.json``, regenerates the
results vertical-slice page ``docs/report_src/generated/rpt001_vertical_slice.md``
from the committed rpt001-v2 analysis artifacts, resolves
``{{jw:include path="..."}}`` directives, and assembles the full report at
``build/capstone/rpt001/report.md``.

Deterministic: no timestamps, no absolute paths, normalized newlines.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/build_capstone.py --profile rpt001
    python3 scripts/build_capstone.py --profile rpt001 --check
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SRC = REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "report_src"
ANALYSIS = REPO_ROOT / "analysis" / "rpt001-v2"
FIGURE_REL = "figures/rpt001-v2/F1_legacy_l1_instrument_results.svg"
GENERATED_HEADER = "<!-- GENERATED by scripts/build_capstone.py; DO NOT EDIT. -->\n"
PROFILE_SCHEMA = "joulewise.report_profile.v1"
SOURCE_MAP_SCHEMA = "joulewise.report_source_map.v1"
LEGACY_LABEL = "legacy L1 (manual review; pre-2M)"

INCLUDE_RE = re.compile(r'^\{\{jw:include path="([^"]+)"\}\}\s*$', re.MULTILINE)
CITATION_RE = re.compile(r"@([A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)")

SEEDED_BIBLIOGRAPHY_IDS = {
    "joulesort2007", "splitwise-isca2024", "distserve", "mooncake",
    "mlperf_power", "zeus", "tokenpowerbench", "mlenergy_benchmark",
    "intelligence_per_watt", "bench360", "chung2026joules",
}
RPT002_SOURCE_IDS = {
    "revisiting-disaggregation-energy-2026", "dualscale-2026",
    "prima-cpp-2025", "splitzip-2026", "systematic-quantization-2025",
    "sustainable-edge-ai-2025", "silicon-showdown-2026",
}
VERIFICATION_STATUSES = {"UNVERIFIED_BY_SESSION", "VERIFIED_AGAINST_PRIMARY"}

REGEN_COMMAND = (
    "python3 scripts/build_capstone.py --profile rpt001 --full --offline "
    "--runs-root runs"
)
CHECK_COMMAND = (
    "python3 scripts/build_capstone.py --profile rpt001 --offline --check"
)

# This report-text scan is only a tripwire; claims_lint phase4 is the gate of record.
FORBIDDEN_PHRASES = [re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE) for p in (
    r"\b(?:more|less)\s+efficient\b", r"\bscales?\s+with\s+model\s+size\b",
    r"\bstatistically\s+significant\b", r"\bclears?\s+the\s+detection\s+floor\b",
    r"\buses?\s+less\s+energy\b", r"\blower\s+energy\s+consumption\b",
    r"\b(?:\d+(?:\.\d+)?\s*[x×]\s+)?energy\s+savings?\b", r"\boutperforms?\b",
    r"\benergy\s+consumption\s+increases?\s+with\s+parameter\s+count\b",
)]


def fail(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"build_capstone: ERROR: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    raise SystemExit(1)


def load_profile() -> dict:
    profile = json.loads((SRC / "report.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if profile.get("schema") != PROFILE_SCHEMA:
        fail(f"unknown report profile schema: {profile.get('schema')!r}")
    chapters = profile.get("chapters", [])
    if not chapters:
        fail("profile lists no chapters")
    if len(set(chapters)) != len(chapters):
        fail("duplicate chapter paths in profile")
    for chapter in chapters:
        p = Path(chapter)
        if p.is_absolute() or ".." in p.parts:
            fail(f"chapter path escapes docs/report_src/: {chapter}")
        if not (SRC / p).is_file():
            fail(f"missing chapter: {chapter}")
    adapter = profile.get("format_adapter", {})
    if adapter.get("renderer") not in (None,):
        fail("format adapter renderer is pending P1-008; only null is accepted")
    return profile


def _profile_file(profile: dict, field: str) -> Path:
    rel = profile.get(field)
    if not isinstance(rel, str) or not rel:
        fail(f"profile has no {field!r} path")
    path = Path(rel)
    if path.is_absolute() or ".." in path.parts:
        fail(f"{field} path escapes docs/report_src/: {rel}")
    target = SRC / path
    if not target.is_file():
        fail(f"missing {field}: {rel}")
    return target


def validate_bibliography(profile: dict) -> None:
    """Validate canonical citation metadata and the RPT-002 source map offline."""
    bibliography_path = _profile_file(profile, "bibliography")
    try:
        bibliography = json.loads(bibliography_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        fail(f"invalid bibliography JSON: {exc}")
    if not isinstance(bibliography, list) or not bibliography:
        fail("bibliography must be a non-empty CSL JSON array")

    by_id = {}
    for index, item in enumerate(bibliography):
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            fail(f"bibliography item {index} is not an object")
        citation_id = item.get("id")
        if not isinstance(citation_id, str) or not citation_id.strip():
            fail(f"bibliography item {index} has no non-empty id")
        if citation_id in by_id:
            fail(f"duplicate bibliography id: {citation_id}")
        for field in ("type", "title"):
            if not isinstance(item.get(field), str) or not item[field].strip():
                fail(f"bibliography item {citation_id} has no non-empty {field}")
        for field in ("DOI", "URL"):
            if field in item and not isinstance(item[field], str):
                fail(f"bibliography item {citation_id} {field} must be a string")
        by_id[citation_id] = item

    missing_seeded = sorted((SEEDED_BIBLIOGRAPHY_IDS | RPT002_SOURCE_IDS) - by_id.keys())
    if missing_seeded:
        fail(f"bibliography is missing required id: {missing_seeded[0]}")

    source_map_path = _profile_file(profile, "source_map")
    try:
        source_map = json.loads(source_map_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
        fail(f"invalid source-map JSON: {exc}")
    if source_map.get("schema") != SOURCE_MAP_SCHEMA:
        fail(f"unknown source-map schema: {source_map.get('schema')!r}")
    sources = source_map.get("sources")
    if not isinstance(sources, list):
        fail("source map sources must be an array")
    mapped_ids = [source.get("id") for source in sources if isinstance(source, dict)]
    if len(mapped_ids) != len(sources) or len(set(mapped_ids)) != len(mapped_ids):
        fail("source map ids must be unique non-empty object fields")
    if set(mapped_ids) != RPT002_SOURCE_IDS:
        fail("source map must contain exactly the seven RPT-002 source ids")
    for source in sources:
        source_id = source["id"]
        if source.get("verification_status") not in VERIFICATION_STATUSES:
            fail(f"source {source_id} has unknown verification_status")
        if source.get("primary_url") != by_id[source_id].get("URL"):
            fail(f"source {source_id} primary_url differs from bibliography URL")
        if not isinstance(source.get("retrieval_date"), str) or not source["retrieval_date"]:
            fail(f"source {source_id} has no retrieval-date placeholder")
        for field in ("claim_role", "evidence_locations", "feeds",
                      "lead_verification_required"):
            value = source.get(field)
            if not value or not isinstance(value, (str, list)):
                fail(f"source {source_id} has no {field}")

    cited = set()
    for chapter in profile["chapters"]:
        cited.update(CITATION_RE.findall((SRC / chapter).read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    unresolved = sorted(cited - by_id.keys())
    if unresolved:
        fail(f"unresolved citation key: {unresolved[0]}")
    unused = sorted(by_id.keys() - cited)
    if unused:
        print(f"build_capstone: WARNING: unused bibliography id: {unused[0]}", file=sys.stderr)


def generate_results_page() -> str:
    claims = json.loads((ANALYSIS / "claims_index.jsonl").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def run_full(runs_root: Path, offline: bool) -> None:
    # All steps are local and stdlib-only; --offline makes that contract explicit.
    figure_cmd = [sys.executable, "scripts/make_figures.py", "--runs-root", str(runs_root),
                  "--input-manifest", "analysis/rpt001-v2/input_manifest.json"]
    if offline:
        figure_cmd.append("--offline")
    subprocess.run(figure_cmd, cwd=REPO_ROOT, check=True)
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, "scripts/claims_lint.py", "--mode", "phase4",
                    "--write-projection"], cwd=REPO_ROOT, check=True)
    verify_artifact_manifest()


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--profile", default="rpt001")
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true",
                    help="Compare regenerated outputs against tracked sources; exit 2 on drift.")
    ap.add_argument("--full", action="store_true",
                    help="Regenerate analysis, lint claims, verify hashes, then assemble.")
    ap.add_argument("--offline", action="store_true",
                    help="Run only the explicitly network-free build path.")
    ap.add_argument("--runs-root", type=Path, default=Path("runs"))
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.profile != "rpt001":
        fail(f"unknown profile: {args.profile}")

    if args.full:
        run_full(args.runs_root, args.offline)
    verify_artifact_manifest()
    profile = load_profile()
    validate_bibliography(profile)
    results_page = generate_results_page()
    gen_path = SRC / "generated" / "rpt001_vertical_slice.md"

    if args.check:
        drift = []
        if not gen_path.is_file() or gen_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != results_page:
            drift.append(str(gen_path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)))
        # Validate assembly from tracked source without treating the untracked
        # build product as a reference. This keeps --check clean-clone safe.
        assemble(profile)
        if drift:
            print(f"build_capstone: DRIFT in {drift[0]}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        print("build_capstone: check OK (no drift)")
        return 0

    gen_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    gen_path.write_text(results_page, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    assembled = assemble(profile)
    out_path = REPO_ROOT / "build" / "capstone" / "rpt001" / "report.md"
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out_path.write_text(assembled, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    digest = hashlib.sha256(assembled.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    print(f"build_capstone: assembled build/capstone/rpt001/report.md sha256={digest}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

Log</h1> <p>This is the canonical record of design decisions for JouleWise. Every decision that binds later work, trades off real alternatives, or would otherwise need to be re-derived by a future agent gets an entry here.</p> <h2 id="how-to-use-this-log">How To Use This Log</h2> <ul> <li>Before implementing anything non-trivial, check whether a decision here already covers it. Do not silently re-decide settled questions.</li> <li>When you make a new decision of this kind during a run, add an entry, link it from the run report, and reference its ID (<code>D-NNN</code>) in the code review or doc that applies it.</li> <li>Statuses: <code>accepted</code> (binding until revisited), <code>open</code> (criteria defined, evidence pending), <code>proposed</code> (recorded, awaiting Ed&#39;s ratification), <code>superseded by D-NNN</code>.</li> <li>Every entry must include Options Considered and Considerations. A decision without recorded alternatives is not auditable.</li> <li>Revisit triggers are part of the contract: when a trigger fires, the decision must be re-examined, not quietly worked around.</li> </ul> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Title</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>D-001</td> <td>Run bundles store normalized <code>config.json</code>, not YAML</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-002</td> <td>Telemetry sampling via subprocess + file, no controller threading</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-003</td> <td>Timestamp and clock-alignment policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-004</td> <td><code>powermetrics</code> privilege workflow</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-005</td> <td>One bundle per repetition, grouped by experiment manifest</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-006</td> <td>Dashboard v1 is a static HTML report generator</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-007</td> <td>YAML config input is deferred</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-008</td> <td>Split runs arrive via schema v0.2 (<code>run_kind</code> + <code>split_plan</code>)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-009</td> <td>Dependency policy: stdlib core, optional extras</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-010</td> <td>Run ID scheme</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-011</td> <td><code>summary_metrics.json</code> is the bundle completion marker</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-012</td> <td>Failure-reason to run-status mapping</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-013</td> <td>Controller-as-DUT mitigation for Mac-local runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-014</td> <td>Statistical protocol for repeated runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-015</td> <td>Split-mechanism priority and same-runtime rule</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-016</td> <td>Benchmark model selection</td> <td>open (provisional small-model pick 2026-07-06; opens 2G only)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-017</td> <td>CI scope</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-018</td> <td>Per-backend <code>power_w</code> definition and rail policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-019</td> <td>Mock adapters use simulated time via an injectable clock</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-020</td> <td>CLI binds <code>FakeClock</code> for all-mock runs, <code>SystemClock</code> otherwise</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-021</td> <td>Controller flushes <code>events.jsonl</code> before the reduce stage</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-022</td> <td>Auto-generated run-ID suffix is config-hash-derived, not random</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-023</td> <td>Per-item phase status lives solely in the exit checklists</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-024</td> <td>Adapters receive a <code>RunContext</code>, not piecemeal parameters</td> <td>accepted; implemented (2N.1, 2026-07-06)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-025</td> <td>One shared bundle read layer for reducer, report, validation, and aggregation</td> <td>accepted; implemented (2N.8, 2026-07-06)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-026</td> <td>Measured window is bounded by sampling-active marker events</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-027</td> <td>Per-rail rows must share per-sample timestamps; pre-Window-A allowlist superseded by D-041/D-042</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-040</td> <td>Suite architecture v2: generic suite mechanism, bundle-level replication</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-041</td> <td>Benchmark interop via frozen-subset imports and marker-shim energy layer; interop lane remains post-2M + post-P2-010a</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-042</td> <td>D-034 implementation lane reopened; suite build may proceed pre-2M</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-043</td> <td>Supersession-closure discipline</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-044</td> <td>Suite config identity: omission-serialized ref + effective-manifest hash</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-045</td> <td>Suite substrate execution semantics (run_suite, statuses, per-item outputs)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-046</td> <td>AP-6 sentinel delivery is ids-native BOS-less at literal equal shape</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-047</td> <td>Affine ladder pins: level set, smoke sizing, gate denominators</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-048</td> <td>Split program is model-first: pre-registered compositional prediction before split runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-049</td> <td>Split transfer-energy boundary accounting on discrete-GPU ends</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-050</td> <td>Active stop cards and process-trace manifests</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-051</td> <td>Advisor status site uses source-derived static pages plus fail-soft live GitHub overlays</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-052</td> <td>Capstone scope contract: frozen umbrella headline and contribution ladder</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-053</td> <td>Contrast-level statistical inference and the frozen analysis registry</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-054</td> <td>False-effect guard floor and unknown-term claim-ceiling policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-055</td> <td>Research-question registry is the canonical live index</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-056</td> <td>Suite order policies and order_row provenance</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-057</td> <td>Uncertainty terms: drift is a bound; idle-subtracted is a labeled within-device secondary view</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-068</td> <td>Site deployment is Ed-manual; sessions end with a drift report, never a deploy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-069</td> <td>Advisor-doc alignment (stream S-0) is sanctioned front-facing work</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-070</td> <td>Architectural-axes extension agenda (AXI): scope, claim posture, batch-axis rulings</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-071</td> <td>G10 memory-fit rule ratified (axi-sd-memory-fit-shape-v1); device-list review opened</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-072</td> <td>Standing self-merge-with-full-gate authority (gh merges included)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-073">D-073</a></td> <td>D-016 device-list amendment: Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-074">D-074</a></td> <td>Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-075">D-075</a></td> <td>Extension-axis intake: ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-076">D-076</a></td> <td>Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review): measured-first budgets</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-077">D-077</a></td> <td>Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log.html#d-078">D-078</a></td> <td>Soundness gate: no claim-bearing extraction from time-anchor-defective powermetrics corpora</td> <td>accepted; operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the full repair arc (close-out cap explicitly Ed-ratified 2026-07-22; original-text ratification rides PR #79 review)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <hr> <blockquote> <p><strong>Site view:</strong> the complete entry index appears above; the 72 older full entries are omitted from this page for capsule size. The complete log is the repository file <a href="https://github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise/blob/main/docs/decision_log.md"><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></a>.</p> </blockquote> <span id="d-073"></span><h2 id="d-073-d-016-device-list-amendment-mac-3080-ti-primary-fleet-12-gib-cap">D-073: D-016 device-list amendment — Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the D-071 brief, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/brief.md</code>). The primary cross-target fleet is the 128 GB M3 Max Mac and the 3080 Ti (12 GiB) rig; the G10 capacity cap re-floors from 8 GiB to <strong>12 GiB</strong> (3080 Ti class sets the floor). Jetson hardware is retained as OPTIONAL, non-cap-setting replication — the edge/8 GiB cell can be added later as a replication row without re-deciding this. The split study&#39;s two nodes are the Mac and the 3080 Ti rig. Big models remain open via the Mac-only subsystem (D-071 clause 3). Follow-ons ruled by Ed same session: (a) conditional primary-model repin remains open with a WIDENED candidate search under the new cap (Ed: &quot;is there really nothing better than Qwen3-1.7B? Gemma 4B or something?&quot;) — 3-4B-class models now fit comfortably; (b) dense/MoE pair re-search under the 12 GiB cap (OLMo dense arm failed G4 as published — see the OLMo verification record in the same trace directory).</p> <span id="d-074"></span><h2 id="d-074-conditional-qwen3-4b-primary-repin-olmo-1b-conversion-spike-authorized">D-074: Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the 12 GiB model search, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/model-search-12gib.md</code>). (1) Qwen3-4B becomes the D-016 primary CONDITIONALLY: the repin lands only when the evidence gates pass (immutable source/license, MLX-Q4/GGUF-Q4/CUDA artifact receipts, three-runtime generation, G10 at the 12 GiB cap, KV receipts, thinking-mode policy pinned); any gate failure retains Qwen2.5-1.5B. New evidence era on success: manifests + quant ladder regenerate from one frozen source revision; Qwen2.5 results preserved as legacy. Runner-up Qwen3-1.7B; Gemma-3-4B rejected for the gated custom license + multimodal MLX seam. (2) The time-boxed OLMo-1B original-format→MLX conversion spike is authorized; success revives the matched OLMoE pair, failure files the dated negative finding and the pair defers (Option C) without re-litigation. Both execute next session as agent-lane work.</p> <span id="d-075"></span><h2 id="d-075-extension-axis-intake-ranked-fold-in-without-new-thesis-proliferation">D-075: Extension-axis intake — ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted (Ed-directed intake via the 2026-07-17 evaluation)</li> <li>Phase: Phase 2+ research program</li> </ul> <p>Context: Ed directed a six-axis evaluation and ratified the resulting roadmap at <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/roadmap-synthesis.md</code>. D-055 keeps C5 deliberation in the bank and the registry as the canonical live index; D-070 keeps these axes as stress tests of Q4, caps candidate commitments at L2, and reserves commitment authority to Ed. The disposition ledger is <code>docs/stream_logs/2026-07-17-axes-foldin.md</code>.</p> <p>Decision:</p> <ol> <li>Admit C5-2.5c as the primary speculative-decoding Q4 break-even rider, C5-2.5b as its proposal-work secondary, and C5-2.5d as a mandatory contamination control. Preserve C5-2.5a in the deliberative bank as a deferred candidate rider only; it is not a standalone campaign commitment before a prospective cross-mechanism design is affordable. All four retain the evaluation&#39;s exact ceilings and forbidden upgrades, and C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY is binding.</li> <li>Admit C5-2.11 as the on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and attach it to C5-2.4, C5-1.12, and C-023-QUALITY-EQUIV-QUANT. Preserve C5-2.12, C5-2.13, and C5-2.14 only as candidate riders on the existing context/KV-growth, prompt-cache/replay, and Q4/AP-1 homes.</li> <li>Admit one new canonical RQ row, RQ-AXI-HYBRID-PAIR, at an L2 named-pair ceiling. Attach the attention/context-slope and module-attribution refinements to existing rows. Record kernel/backend provenance as amendments to C5-1.8, C5-2.7, and C5-3.3, not new theses.</li> <li>Keep the roadmap&#39;s do-not-fold set out of the canonical row set. Its negative dispositions and all unresolved feasibility questions remain in the stream ledger, including explicit <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> markers. Intake does not convert an unresolved runtime, model-pair, adapter, or device-fit question into a capstone commitment.</li> </ol> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Mint every evaluated suggestion as an independent live question. Rejected: it duplicates existing homes, imports unidentifiable mechanism claims, and violates D-070&#39;s single-Q4-thesis posture.</li> <li>Admit only the top three ranked items. Rejected: the lower-cost controls, riders, and provenance amendments prevent predictable attribution errors without creating independent theses.</li> <li>Apply the roadmap&#39;s ranked fold-in and explicit exclusions. Chosen by Ed.</li> </ol> <p>Considerations: this is research-agenda intake, not campaign scheduling or evidence promotion. Every admitted candidate/rider remains floor-gated, earliest-phase tagged, capped at L2 unless an already-existing parent row&#39;s separate machinery says otherwise, and subject to its named forbidden upgrade. The published corpus remains claim-evidence-flagged; no fixture, runtime feasibility result, or registry entry is live energy evidence. D-070 remains the authority for Ed&#39;s axis commitments and quiet-Mac ordering.</p> <p>Revisit triggers: a relevant <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> feasibility finding lands; a named runtime/pair becomes unsupported; P2-015 floors make a predeclared effect undetectable; or Ed changes the D-070 commitment set. Revisit by amending the owning row and this decision&#39;s ledger, never by silently promoting an excluded candidate.</p> <span id="d-076"></span><h2 id="d-076-site-capacity-right-sizing-aud-wo-039-review-measured-first-budgets">D-076: Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review) — measured-first budgets</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-17/18. Owner: lead under Ed&#39;s &quot;host the brief&quot; directive (the capacity decision event AUD-WO-039 fenced on). Ruling, encoded in tests with PR #76: the 1 MiB Lakebed hard cap is inviolate; the measured-artifact budget is 1,000,000 B (measured mode via the pinned validator, SITE-02 loud-discovery discipline); the 943,718 B conservative-estimate guard remains ONLY as fallback when measured mode is unavailable (estimator overshoot documented ~4.3% on identical input). WO-039 preservation boundary held: no advisor-facing page, navigation, provenance, or deep link trimmed. Current measured artifact 961,210 B. Revisit trigger: measured artifact within 24 KB of the hard cap forces the next right-sizing review before any addition.</p> <span id="d-077"></span><h2 id="d-077-environment-guard-idle-admission-and-cooldown-v2">D-077: Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Phase: 2 / measurement</li> </ul> <p>Context: a Ventura video screensaver compositing on an awake display was identified as a material, repeatable contaminant. The affected windows showed about 50% GPU duty and were already detected by the existing <code>idle_window_suspect</code> thresholds. The campaign preflight, per-run admission, and D-014 cooldown nevertheless lacked one shared environment policy, exact override custody, and a sustained-window implementation. In particular, the old cooldown could release after one 5-second sub-window even though the contract called for a rolling 30-second recovery window.</p> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Treat doctor output as a quietness certificate and continue to rely on operator judgment between members. Rejected: a point-in-time advisory cannot certify the later measured window and cannot enforce fixed-n admission.</li> <li>Change persistent display/screensaver preferences or allow contaminated members to be skipped or waived. Rejected: campaign preparation must not mutate host policy, and outcome-dependent skipping/waiving would break the fixed-n design and conceal the contamination.</li> <li>Use a hash-bound campaign-policy sidecar, an enforcing campaign preflight, per-run idle admission with one evidence-bearing retry, and cooldown v2 with frozen clean-anchor fallback. Chosen.</li> </ol> <p>Decision:</p> <ul> <li>A shared pure evaluator owns environment findings. Doctor consumes it only advisorily. <code>run_campaign.py</code> consumes it enforcingly after taking the campaign lock and before member 1. Critical unknowns fail closed. Load average is recorded as evidence but is never a member-admission gate.</li> <li>The production quiet-Mac policy requires AC power with an externally connected source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Quiet-mode arming is explicit and transient: countdown, <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, then a complete re-probe. Persistent settings are never changed.</li> <li>An environment override must name the exact snapshot and findings digests it acknowledges. It is recorded as an override, never a waiver, and makes every resulting member universally claim-ineligible.</li> <li>Per-run idle admission reuses the validated <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code> threshold. It permits exactly one fully evidenced retry with distinct raw artifacts. Persistent awake-display, screensaver, or unknown critical state aborts immediately. Production aborts after retry; the exploratory-only <code>flag</code> path completes the fixed-n member but stamps the unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> reason on gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims. There is no skip action.</li> <li>Cooldown v2 amends D-014: recovery requires a complete, duration-weighted, sustained 30-second evidence window; the one-sided rule is <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code>, so a below-reference window is recovered. Nominal thermal state is conjunctive. A calibrated absolute ceiling, when configured, is only an additional upper cap. A preceding baseline is reference-eligible only when its idle window is clean, critical environment checks passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. Otherwise the campaign uses one frozen clean anchor (NEG-8 reference start when present, else the first admission-passing baseline), records its provenance, never updates it from later outcomes, and fails closed when no eligible reference or anchor exists. Historical recovered rows are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>The policy owner is a strictly typed, byte-hashed sidecar under <code>configs/campaign_policies/</code>; policy version and SHA-256 are copied into each governed bundle. Campaign execution defaults to the production sidecar. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy non-enforcing behavior. All bundle/config additions are nullable or omission-serialized; legacy normalized config bytes and hashes are unchanged.</li> <li>This amends D-057&#39;s stable claim-reason vocabulary by adding <code>environment_admission_failed</code> and <code>environment_override</code>. Both are universal and unwaivable for gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</li> </ul> <p>Considerations: environment admission is measurement-apparatus integrity, not post-hoc data cleaning. Duration weighting prevents irregular sub-window cadence from manufacturing coverage. Frozen-anchor provenance prevents a contaminated or outcome-selected member from quietly becoming the campaign&#39;s new recovery reference. The doctor remains useful as an early advisor without claiming more than its snapshot can prove.</p> <p>Consequences: campaign and bundle contracts gain policy/preflight/admission provenance, environment snapshots gain nullable display/screensaver/HID fields plus a post-run observation, and D-014&#39;s recovery wording is governed by cooldown v2 for new evidence. This decision is separate from AUD-WO-033, which remains behavior-preserving; D-077 intentionally changes future measurement admission and cooldown behavior and does not reinterpret sealed historical bundles.</p> <p>Revisit when: live quiet-window validation contradicts the defensive <code>pmset -g systemstate</code> display parser; calibrated platform data justifies an absolute ceiling; or a new platform cannot expose an equivalent critical probe without privilege.</p> <p>Fix-round amendment (2026-07-18): review found that summing sub-window durations as the completeness test made small inter-probe gaps reject an otherwise complete wall-clock window. Cooldown v2 now requires both a retained wall-clock span of at least <code>sustained_window_s</code> and captured coverage of at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code>, with <code>coverage_fraction</code> defaulting to 0.8 and recorded in thresholds, trace rows, and release evidence. The same fix round made the existing frozen-reference rule operational for controller repetitions, attached cooldown evidence to each physical repetition (and each AXI entry), froze the first eligible repetition in execution order, re-probed the full governed environment per repetition, and added a guard observation after every idle capture. Environment-preflight early exits now retain a terminal campaign verdict; missing screensaver defaults domains use the macOS 20-minute default; and the two D-077 claim barriers are registered in the canonical reducer vocabulary. These are defect corrections to the accepted policy, not new policy alternatives.</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <a href="decision_log.html">Recent</a> · <strong aria-current="page">Archive 1</strong></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

<!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent.
