delta re-audit caught a LEAD-pinned predictor defect (8th fix-rounds-inject-defects datum, first lead-authored); AXI-SD memo: OLMo pair d_active 0.0016 + 8GB-fit may moot Option A&#39;s premise, Qwen3 pair confirmed-fails G10 (17.17 GB) |</p> <hr> <h2 id="full-entry">Full entry</h2> <h2>C-028: C-027 adjudication and integration arc — infrastructure wave, PRs #49/#54/#55, and the integration window (2026-07-10/11)</h2> <p>Full record: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-11-c028-continuation.md</code>; binding rulings: <code>docs/specs/c027/ADJUDICATION.md</code>. No tracked <code>docs/process_traces/</code> artifact is present in this checkout; the run report&#39;s aggregate invocation record is therefore the durable evidence available for this arc, and D-064 governs future tracked event streams. This limitation is recorded rather than repaired with an invented pointer. The arc&#39;s earlier segment (adjudication rounds, PRs #41–#48) is recorded in the CP-5/checkpoint records and stop-card history; this entry records the 2026-07-10/11 continuation.</p> <p>Participants: Fable lead; gpt-5.6-sol as implementer, reviewer, refuter, auditor, and design consultant across ~57 recorded invocations. The lead retained worktree/merge authority, every final diff gate, all live verification, and bookkeeping.</p> <p>Scope of this segment: PR #49 (NV-GATE-2 code-now + flake root-causes) merged <code>1b0f1f6</code> + <code>10e0ad2</code>; PR #54 (P2-041 vetted rebuild from the RED-tranche triage recipe, review + fix round + delta review) merged <code>69a3393</code>; PR #55 (P2-044 idle dependence / HAC / ESS, design-consult-first, review + fix round) merged <code>56d103e</code>. At the Ed-directed pause (stop card checkpoint #4 + amendments) PRs #50–#53 and #56–#58 stood open and lead-gated with the resume order pinned; after resume, the integration tree (<code>c028-integration</code> @ <code>190a0fc</code>, main post-#55 + 7 branches) caught 38 cross-stream failures, the fix round + cross-stream review cleared them, and the full wave merged SHA-guarded (#50, #51, #52, #53, #56, #57, #58 — P2-037 last), with final main verified green and content-identical to the reviewed tree; follow-up PR #59 (from the cross-stream review) is under review and DOC-008 rounds remain in flight. Delegation infrastructure landed on main: adapter, codex-run-v3, usage guard, scope backstop.</p> <p>Closeout amendment (2026-07-11): C-028 is <strong>CLOSED</strong>. PRs #41-#58 are merged; current main&#39;s canonical suite is 1,220 OK (<code>skipped=10</code>) and the corpus gate is 6/6. PR #59 remains open with a 1,224-test green worktree replay (<code>skipped=12</code>), and <code>impl/doc008-kernel</code> is pushed awaiting PR. These open follow-ups do not reopen the card. Every Window-A software gate and P0-003 are satisfied; quiet-machine execution with Ed remains deliberately separate from landed-software status. NVIDIA/Orin protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL pending live evidence.</p> <p>Layer structure: Sol implementation sessions (xhigh; 2 ultra for the p2041-vetted composition and the P2-037 engine) → review lenses (contract + semantics per stream) → severity-tiered refuters (2 per blocker) → independent post-hoc audits (P2-037) → delta re-audits after fix rounds → lead gates (live runs, arithmetic checks, final heads, CI) → cross-stream integration tree before each merge.</p> <p>Unique catches per layer (D-061 evaluation record):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Sol merge review:</strong> caught the lead&#39;s own merge-resolution error — the branch&#39;s updated P2-005 row silently lost by a whole-file <code>--theirs</code> checkout during the #49 conflict resolution; repaired as a proper 3-way merge (<code>13f6c9e</code>). Only layer to catch it.</li> <li><strong>Refuter tier:</strong> narrowed 2 blockers via CONTRADICTORY paired verdicts — P2-041 B1 (contract refuter confirmed, reachability refuter refuted the broad form → landed as the narrowed shared fail-closed cooldown verifier, <code>f2c4701</code>) and P2-037 F1 (design vs repro refuters split the same way → F1 narrowed before the fix round). The disagreement itself was the signal; neither single refuter would have produced the narrowed form.</li> <li><strong>Delta re-audits:</strong> 2 fresh blockers in paths newly reachable only after the fix round (P2-037 delta re-audit: blocker=2/should-fix=3), plus the recurring symlink pattern — cooldown provenance <code>Path.resolve</code> unwrapped against symlink loop/OSError, wrapped fail-closed with a cross-version regression test (<code>5f1f161</code>). Neither finding existed in the pre-fix tree; the re-audit layer is what sees post-fix reachability.</li> <li><strong>Lead gates:</strong> P2-044 F1 cadence arithmetic verified directly (all-intervals population; binding Qwen-r3 values asserted exactly: median 0.1199250625, ratio 1.0581313969 — <code>dc1ab95</code>); live NV-5 localhost gate 3/3 OK closing the open lead gate on #49 (<code>10e0ad2</code>); live doctor run. All three are lead-live-only — no static layer could produce them.</li> <li><strong>Integration tree:</strong> 38 pre-merge cross-stream test failures caught at the combined head, dominated by REPRO-002&#39;s fail-closed environment/inventory checks meeting post-cut fields from sibling streams. Zero of these were visible in any single stream&#39;s green suite.</li> <li><strong>Enforcement layer (scope backstop, live):</strong> 2 bytecode false-positive firings tuned same-day; NEEDS_SCOPE compliant stops ×3 (p2037 fix round, doc008 ×2) — each returning the correct paths where the lead had guessed wrong.</li> </ul> <p>Scope enforcement fired in production: two sessions (p2043-impl, p2044-fixround) exited SCOPE_VIOLATION with work preserved in evidence bundles, not landed; one wrapper crash (lead in-place edit of the installed runner mid-run) was recovered via a lead-authored recovery row rather than a mutated record — both behaviors are now ratified in D-064.</p> <p>Rough spend (from the two manifests + local usage accounting; estimates, not billing truth): 2 ultra sessions ≈ 100M tokens (p2041-vetted composition, P2-037 engine); 53 recorded xhigh invocations (14 v2-manifest + 37 v3-event-stream + 2 transition-era rows) — local 24h accounting shows 50 xhigh sessions ≈ 171M tokens; 2 high (both FAILED rc=1 resume attempts, work recovered in later sessions) ≈ 40M. Fable lead: ~1.8M generation / ~14.8M billed-ish / ~570M cache reads. Two v3 sessions (doc008-r3, pr59-review) still RUNNING at the manifest snapshot.</p> <p>Spend snapshot addendum (2026-07-11 ~20:00Z, <code>codex-usage</code> 24h window, arc-close truth for the table above; estimates, not billing): 59 Sol sessions / 330.6M tokens / ~17.5h session time — xhigh 55 ≈ 190.4M, ultra 2 ≈ 100.3M, high 2 ≈ 40.0M (both FAILED). Composition (measured from raw session records): ~97.4% of Sol input is cached, output ≈ 0.37% of volume. API-list-price equivalent (GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30, cached $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1): Sol ≈ $240, Fable ≈ $810 — combined ≈ $1,050 for the recorded arc; upper bound ≈ $2,300 counting all local Codex sessions (includes non-manifest sessions; resume rows may double-count). Note the inversion: Sol is ~180x the token volume but Fable is ~3.4x the cost — cache reads dominate the lead&#39;s footprint. Snapshot convention now standing in the council skill §Recording + instrumentation.</p> <p>Process artifacts adopted this arc (ratified as/alongside D-064):</p> <ul> <li><strong>claude-codex-report/v1</strong> — canonical machine-parsed session report envelope; run_finished rows record parse validity, finding counts, verification counts, scope flags.</li> <li><strong>codex-run-v3</strong> — append-only event-stream manifest (run_started/run_finished/run_consumed), retry-with-resume, lead-authored recovery rows on wrapper failure.</li> <li><strong>WRITE_SCOPE backstop</strong> — post-run diff vs declared scope; exit 77 + evidence bundle on violation; NEEDS_SCOPE prospective-only expansion (AGENTS.md precedence section, <code>9ca89cc</code>).</li> <li><strong>NEEDS_RULING</strong> — any blocking non-delegable decision early-returns a structured question instead of a guess (<code>31b3f5e</code>); usage guard + usage-pressure mode active.</li> <li><strong>Design-consult-by-default</strong> — Ed-prompted global-rule amendment; exercised for P2-044 (HAC/ESS design consult, <code>827df12</code>) before implementation.</li> </ul> <p>Dissents overridden: none unresolved. The P2-041 RED tranche (ultra round deleting P2-038/P2-040 wholesale) was not landed or argued — it was triaged per-file and rebuilt from main under three Ed-approved C rulings (<code>96e10bd</code>, <code>750f7d0</code>).</p> <p>Calibration note (model-version scoping, per C-027): the refuter contradictory-verdict pattern produced correct narrowings twice; the two scope violations and one thin-output ultra warning are the arc&#39;s recorded 5.6-sol failure modes. Sealed A/B remains the gate before any delegation-boundary change.</p> <h2 id="c-031-d-078-p0-instrument-repair-close-out-session-round-8-landing-round-9-final-confirmation-sign-off-2026-07-22">C-031: D-078 P0 instrument-repair close-out session — round-8 landing, round-9 final confirmation, sign-off (2026-07-22)</h2> <p>Shape: lead resumed the paused arc cold from scratchpad pointers; collected the checkpointed Sol round-8 fix wave; §C-028 delta re-audit (3 fresh read-only Sol lenses over a shared packet → 8 xhigh refuter verdicts, blockers 2 refuters with distinct lenses); Sol xhigh round-8b fix wave under enforced WRITE_SCOPE (one NEEDS_SCOPE early-return, lead-ruled, fixture fix applied at the bench); bounded 8b delta re-audit; lead full-suite gates (2081 → 2088 passed, 0 failures); commit <code>040ca3a</code>; round-9 FINAL confirmation (Sol xhigh review genre); CR9-1 adjudicated as registered limitation L1 per the loop-termination doctrine; close-out <code>debc6d2</code>; PR #79 opened for Ed-named merge.</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li>Sol review lenses: A1 (v3 claim-eligibility contract divergence), B1 (ClockStamp physical-sanity gap → understated B_fiducial ~3 µs), C1/C2 (boundary float, OverflowError escape), C3/C4 (test-wiring gaps).</li> <li>Sol xhigh refuters: killed A2/B2 outright (both plausible, both wrong — A2&#39;s &quot;legacy records break&quot; was self-invalid synthetic-only; B2&#39;s stale-vs-invalid relabel would have broken a ratified distinction); narrowed C1 to a registered nit; split on A1 (contract-confirmed, reachability-refuted) — lead synthesis: pre-existing defense-in-depth hardening, not a round-8 regression.</li> <li>Round-9 confirmation: CR9-1 (floor artifacts self-attesting) — the only finding of the round, repro-backed, lead-reproduced at the bench.</li> <li>Lead unique: false-attribution triage of the 8b audit&#39;s two &quot;blockers&quot; (both were the lead&#39;s own authorized bench edits); the L1 adjudication.</li> </ul> <p>Failure modes recorded: (1) upstream cyber-content filter killed 3/8 refuters mid-run on adversarial phrasing (&quot;malformed/tamper/escape&quot;) — rephrasing as data-quality QA of our own instrument recovered all three (route: keep refuter briefs mechanism-neutral); (2) lead bench-edited the worktree while an enforced-scope Sol session ran in it → false SCOPE_VIOLATION attribution + resume-registry loss (rule: no lead edits in a tree with a live enforced-scope session); (3) the known xhigh review-genre null-final-message mode recurred on round 9; the documented bridge-resume recovery worked first try.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: the 8b delta auditor&#39;s should-fix (OverflowError normalization also reaching v1 replay error behavior) was overridden by lead ruling — frozen-replay doctrine protects computed semantics of parsable artifacts, not crash reproduction on impossible inputs; the reducer&#39;s structured-failure contract governs all protocols.</p> <h2 id="c-032-neg-8-estimand-debate-peer-disagreement-adopted-ed-ratification-2026-07-24">C-032: NEG-8 estimand debate — peer disagreement adopted, Ed ratification (2026-07-24)</h2> <p>Ed directed a formal cross-model debate on the clause-10 ruling before ratifying. Shape: lead position paper + explicit license and request to disagree; one xhigh peer round evaluating five design options plus a peer-proposed sixth; lead adjudication; plain-language synthesis to Ed; Ed ratified the amended design with recorded guardrails (decision log clause-10 addendum). Yield: the peer&#39;s structural correction (anomaly screen must not erase drift from the claim budget) was adopted — the second recorded case of invited peer design judgment beating the lead&#39;s ruling. The debate also surfaced one gap neither model had specced (drift-bound freshness horizon — prompted by Ed&#39;s own risk question) and one open science question (a7-vs-a5 prefill floor scatter, 3x). Calibration note: invited-disagreement debate briefs (steelman each option, demand failure modes + examiner view) produced markedly higher design yield than review-shaped prompts; adopt as the default shape for estimand/contract rulings.</p> <h2>C-033: NEG-8 screen+budget audit gauntlet — a new refuter pairing under A/B, four audit rounds, PR #85 (2026-07-24/25)</h2> <p>Shape: the Ed-ratified SCREEN + BUDGET wave (D-078 clause 10) was taken through four adversarial audit rounds (fresh read-only Sol per round; rounds 1–3 xhigh, round 4 high) with per-severity refuter tiers using a NEW pairing under evaluation — <strong>Opus-contract + Sol-execution distinct lenses</strong> (Ed-directed A/B; now the recorded default per the instrument-mix-authority memory). Three Sol fix rounds (xhigh, xhigh + a high alignment pass, high) plus lead bench fixes closed the findings; two lead-owned decision-log addenda were written at the bench between rounds. Commit stack on main(<code>125a48d</code>): <code>b120d07</code> wave → <code>69b65e5</code> addendum 2 → <code>ad75542</code> fix round 1 → <code>315810a</code> addendum 3 → <code>a5a7acf</code> capsule trim → <code>907ee58</code> fix round 2 → <code>dbf6339</code> fix round 3 → <code>19e15d9</code> assertion restore → <code>60b12af</code> capsule pagination → merged <code>c3e2647</code> (PR #85, 56 files, +6012/−439).</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Auditor (fresh Sol, per round):</strong> found real mechanisms in every round — round 1: estimand-dispatch downgrade (row shape selects the legacy gross-only evaluator), allowance fail-open (missing allowances silently become no allowance), anchor-gate bypass on the existing-bundle re-verdict path, and the refusal-registry gap (the authoritative registry test actually failed on <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code>); round 2: coordinated-downgrade v2 (strip basis <em>and</em> the whole drift group together) and the mock-label seam (<code>telemetry_source=&quot;mock&quot;</code> defeats both dispatch and the anchor gate); round 3: TypeError on malformed basis values, telemetry-triangle downgrade into the frozen arm at the whole-window barrier, and loss of nonempty positive-path integration coverage; round 4: two omitted assertions in the replacement companion (nonempty affected-contrast set, <code>n == 5</code>). BUT it severity-inflated repeatedly — of 7 blocker-tier claims across rounds 1–2, refuter synthesis sustained 3–4 at tier (round 3 and round 4 produced no blockers at all: three should-fix, then one).</li> <li><strong>Opus-contract refuter (unique):</strong> F2 collapse (the &quot;broken frozen replay&quot; blocker rested on a misreading of the freshness addendum&#39;s scoping — landed as a documented superseded gross-only wire, not a code fix); F6 refutation (condition-level distinctness was already contract-discharged at the consumer boundary); G1 re-price (the full-strip variant is a subclass of registered limitation L1, whose closure is queued as FLOOR-BIND-01, not a fresh blocker); G2 re-price (the ratified non-mock carve-out plus D-030&#39;s strict/raw-evidence binding bound the exposure); blast-radius refutation of the auditor&#39;s proposed G2 fixture fix (strict validation binds backend raw evidence, so the naive fix breaks legitimate fixtures); <strong>A1 terminal-mock-bar gap — the session&#39;s best catch</strong>: an <em>honest</em> mock member could reach claim evidence with all mock-exempted barriers disabled, no attacker required; the NEG-8 sentinel route on round-3 F2 (the one route with no downstream catch); and the F3 fixture-fix refutation (a production-promoted fixture cannot be strict-valid — use a patch idiom instead).</li> <li><strong>Sol-execution refuter (unique):</strong> discovery of the coordinated-downgrade <em>variants</em> (strip the drift group and restore the headline floors and the record validates clean — reproduced on the repo fixture, gate <code>20.799350577898302 → 20.399350577898304</code>, exactly the fixture&#39;s 0.4 J allowance; asymmetric removal from the comparative record alone also validates clean); the G2A adjacent blocker (the reduce layer independently trusts metadata/summary mockness in the environment and CPU-admission barriers, so fresh re-reduction reproduces the forged exemption and strict stored-vs-fresh comparison is not a backstop); identification of the authoritative mockness source (custody-bound <code>config().hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bound through <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>); the <code>mock:*</code> tagged-source class caveat (<code>axi_valid_burst</code> config <code>mock</code> vs summary <code>mock:target</code> — compare backend <em>class</em>, not raw strings); and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); the capsule shard-budget trim (<code>a5a7acf</code>) and the pagination ruling that followed (deterministic <code>D-NNN</code> pagination + D-076 artifact-cap redirects); the battery-flake adjudications; and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Re-priced by refuters before fixing: 4 of those (r1 F4 blocker→should-fix; r2 G1/G2 blocker→should-fix; r1 F2 blocker→docs-only, landed as contract clarification). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-moe-routing-energy.md:5155:./docs/site/research.html:17:</header> <main> <section class="learn-hero"> <div class="kicker">Interactive field guide · programming knowledge assumed · measurement science taught here</div> <p class="readme-eyebrow">From watts to warranted claims.</p> <h1>How do you measure<br>a machine thinking?</h1> <p class="lede">You already know how programs execute. This guide adds the uncomfortable part: deciding which physical signal belongs to the program, how much noise the instrument adds, and what the evidence actually permits you to say.</p> <nav class="chapter-nav" aria-label="Guide chapters"> <a href="#hard">The hard part</a><a href="#units">Watts &amp; joules</a> <a href="#sampling">Sampling</a><a href="#bundles">Bundles</a> <a href="#floor">Detection floors</a><a href="#found">Findings</a> <a href="#next">Next</a> </nav> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>measurement_methodology.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 6d80039</span></span> <span class="source-chip" title="docs/site_src/research.html · commit 05002b1"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>site_src/<wbr>research.html</span><span class="source-commit">commit 05002b1</span></span></div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="hard"> <div class="chapter-number">01</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">Why this is hard</div> <h2>The model does not come with an energy return value.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">A profiler can tell you which function consumed CPU time. Energy is a physical quantity observed through a separate instrument. You have to align two clocks, define a boundary, and decide what else was happening while the model ran.</p> <div class="concept-grid"> <article><span>Boundary</span><h3>Which power?</h3><p>SoC rails omit parts of the whole machine. Wall power includes more than the chip. Neither is automatically wrong; an unlabeled boundary is.</p></article> <article><span>Attribution</span><h3>Which interval?</h3><p>Load the model too late or stop sampling too early and the number answers a different question than the experiment config asked.</p></article> <article><span>Workload</span><h3>Which work?</h3><p>Prompt length, generated tokens, batching, caching, stop behavior, and content can all change the physical execution.</p></article> <article><span>Noise</span><h3>Which difference?</h3><p>Background activity, thermal state, sampling cadence, clock error, and run order can manufacture a small “effect.”</p></article> </div> <aside class="learn-aside"><strong>The measurement-science move:</strong> replace “I got a number” with “I defined a quantity, captured the evidence, bounded what could imitate it, and stated the claim ceiling.”</aside> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="units"> <div class="chapter-number">02</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">Watts, joules, and idle</div> <h2>Power is a rate. Energy is the area.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">A watt is one joule per second. If power changes over time, energy is the integral under the power trace. That identity is a unit definition—not a JouleWise measurement result.</p> <div class="equation-stack"> <div><span>instantaneous power</span><strong>P(t)</strong><small>watts = joules / second</small></div> <div><span>gross measured energy</span><strong>E = ∫ P(t) dt</strong><small>headline basis within the named boundary</small></div> <div><span>idle-subtracted energy</span><strong>E<sub>secondary</sub> = ∫ (P(t) − P<sub>idle</sub>) dt</strong><small>within-device secondary view only</small></div> </div> <p>Idle is not “free energy to erase.” It is an observed baseline under a stated condition. Subtracting it can help describe activity above baseline on one device, but it can distort comparisons: a high-idle device gets a larger subtraction. JouleWise therefore uses <strong>gross energy for every cross-device, cross-configuration, and split-vs-monolithic headline</strong>. Phase energy is gross-only.</p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>measurement_methodology.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 6d80039</span></span></div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="sampling"> <div class="chapter-number">03</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">How powermetrics sampling works</div> <h2>You never see the continuous curve.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede"><code>powermetrics</code> reports discrete samples from named Apple power rails. JouleWise aligns those samples with runtime events and integrates between explicit measured-window boundaries. Move the toy controls below: the underlying program is unchanged, but the estimated area changes when the window or sample pattern changes.</p> <div class="interactive-card" data-trace-lab> <div class="interactive-head"><div><span class="card-label">Toy trace · illustrative, not project evidence</span><h3>Drag the window and sample controls.</h3></div><span class="status-chip amber">local-only SVG + JS</span></div> <svg class="power-lab" viewBox="0 0 720 290" role="img" aria-labelledby="traceTitle traceDesc"> <title id="traceTitle">Interactive toy power trace</title> <desc data-count-out>—</strong></div> </div> <p class="interactive-note">The orange curve is an invented signal. Cyan dots are discrete samples; the shaded band is the measured window. Real JouleWise bundles retain the trace and event markers so the integration can be replayed rather than trusted.</p> </div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="bundles"> <div class="chapter-number">04</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">Strict validation and bundles</div> <h2>A bundle is a proof packet, not a CSV export.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">The run directory is deliberately boring: normalized configuration, metadata, timestamped events, raw power evidence, logs, model outputs, and summary metrics. The interesting part is what strict validation does with it.</p> <div class="bundle-diagram" role="img" aria-label="Run bundle artifacts flow through strict validation to a bounded claim"> <div class="bundle-box"><span>run bundle</span><code>config.json</code><code>metadata.json</code><code>events.jsonl</code><code>raw telemetry</code><code>outputs + logs</code><code>summary metrics</code></div> <div class="bundle-arrow">replay →</div> <div class="bundle-box validator-box"><span>strict validator</span><p>parse raw evidence</p><p>re-derive windows</p><p>recompute energy</p><p>check provenance</p><p>fail on mismatch</p></div> <div class="bundle-arrow">gate →</div> <div class="bundle-box claim-box"><span>claim ceiling</span><p>L0: auditability</p><p>L1: descriptive</p><p>L2+: only after floor, uncertainty, plan, and evidence gates</p></div> </div> <p><strong>Strict-valid does not mean scientifically conclusive.</strong> It means the recorded artifact is internally valid under the strict contract. A bundle can be strict-valid and still carry flags that prevent a comparison claim. That distinction matters in the newest floor data.</p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md · commit db150a0"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>claims_ladder.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit db150a0</span></span></div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="floor"> <div class="chapter-number">05</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">Detection floors</div> <h2>How small is too small to resolve?</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">Repeat the same condition and the measured energy moves anyway. The false-effect guard floor summarizes how large that repeat scatter—or an ABBA comparison artifact—can look. An effect below the applicable floor is <strong>not resolvable</strong>, not proven absent.</p> <div class="interactive-card floor-lab" data-floor-lab> <div class="interactive-head"><div><span class="card-label">Effect-versus-floor gate</span><h3>Try to clear a real verified floor.</h3></div><span class="status-chip">calibration logic</span></div> <label class="floor-select">Choose the applicable gate <select data-floor-select> <option value="0.527197" data-basis="gross request · absolute repeat">Gross mid-request absolute · 0.527197 J</option> <option value="0.909237" data-basis="gross request · comparative ABBA">Gross mid-request comparative · 0.909237 J</option> <option value="0.536632" data-basis="idle-subtracted request · within-device secondary">Idle-subtracted mid-request absolute · 0.536632 J</option> <option value="0.894215" data-basis="idle-subtracted request · within-device secondary comparative">Idle-subtracted mid-request comparative · 0.894215 J</option> <option value="1.738940" data-basis="gross prefill phase · governing gate">Gross prefill phase gate · 1.738940 J</option> <option value="1.026892" data-basis="gross decode phase · governing gate">Gross decode phase gate · 1.026892 J</option> <option value="4.922865" data-basis="gross suite-item · governing gate">Gross suite-item gate · 4.922865 J</option> <option value="24.618735" data-basis="gross suite-level · governing gate">Gross suite-level gate · 24.618735 J</option> </select> </label> <label class="effect-control">Hypothetical observed effect <input data-effect type="range" min="0" max="30" value="0.70" step="0.01"> <output data-effect-out>0.70 J</output> </label> <div class="floor-track" aria-hidden="true"><span data-floor-mark></span><i data-effect-mark></i></div> <div class="floor-verdict" data-floor-verdict aria-live="polite"></div> <p class="interactive-note">Clearing this numeric gate is necessary, not sufficient. It does not clear clock, sampling, uncertainty, contamination, multiplicity, correctness, or pre-registered analysis-plan gates.</p> </div> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/phase_2/detection_floor.md · commit 907ee58"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>phase_2/<wbr>detection_floor.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 907ee58</span></span></div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="found"> <div class="chapter-number">06</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">What the project has found so far</div> <h2>Real floors, plus an important warning.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">The verified Window-A extraction reports the following false-effect guard floors. Comparative values use ABBA blocks; “gate” is the larger applicable absolute/comparative value. Every energy number states its D-067 basis.</p> <div class="table-scroll"> <table class="ledger measurement-table learn-floor-table"> <thead><tr><th>window</th><th>energy basis</th><th>verified floor</th><th>how to read it</th></tr></thead> <tbody> <tr><td>mid request · absolute</td><td>gross · headline</td><td>0.527197 J</td><td>repeat-scatter floor</td></tr> <tr><td>mid request · comparative</td><td>gross · headline</td><td>0.909237 J</td><td>ABBA comparison floor</td></tr> <tr><td>mid request · absolute</td><td>idle-subtracted · within-device secondary</td><td>0.536632 J</td><td>repeat-scatter floor</td></tr> <tr><td>mid request · comparative</td><td>idle-subtracted · within-device secondary</td><td>0.894215 J</td><td>ABBA comparison floor</td></tr> <tr><td>prefill phase</td><td>gross · phase basis</td><td>1.738940 J</td><td>governing gate</td></tr> <tr><td>decode phase</td><td>gross · phase basis</td><td>1.026892 J</td><td>governing gate</td></tr> <tr><td>suite item</td><td>gross · headline</td><td>4.922865 J</td><td>governing gate</td></tr> <tr><td>suite level</td><td>gross · headline</td><td>24.618735 J</td><td>governing gate</td></tr> </tbody> </table> </div> <aside class="evidence-warning"><strong>The warning is part of the result.</strong> The floor collection is strict-valid and collection-usable, yet every contributing bundle is claim-evidence flagged. Universal clock-bound and in-window-sample flags, plus drift/cooldown concerns in several comparative cells, mean these values are calibration evidence pending adjudication—not a license for an L2/L3 comparison claim.</aside> <p class="source-path">Cited artifact: <a href="https://github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise/blob/main/docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-floor-extraction/extraction-verified.json"><code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-floor-extraction/extraction-verified.json</code></a> </p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-floor-extraction/extraction-verified.json · commit b28c895"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>process_traces/<wbr>2026-07-17-floor-extraction/<wbr>extraction-verified.json</span><span class="source-commit">commit b28c895</span></span></div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="next"> <div class="chapter-number">07</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">What comes next</div> <h2>Turn calibration into governed comparisons.</h2> <div class="next-grid"> <article><span>Adjudicate</span><h3>Resolve the evidence flags.</h3><p>Decide whether clock-bound, cadence, drift, and cooldown evidence allows these floors to govern later claims or requires a revised capture.</p></article> <article><span>Baseline</span><h3>Run the controlled Mac campaign.</h3><p>Use counterbalanced order, fixed workloads, strict-valid bundles, and the applicable floor gates before interpreting model differences.</p></article> <article><span>Stress</span><h3>Test the energy model.</h3><p>Batching, speculative decoding, MoE versus dense execution, quantization, and reasoning length probe where the fixed-plus-marginal model holds or breaks.</p></article> <article><span>Extend</span><h3>Add hardware without changing honesty.</h3><p>Remote NVIDIA and Orin paths remain provisional until live contact. Cross-device headlines stay gross-first and boundary-labeled.</p></article> </div> <div class="research-questions"> <h3>The research arc</h3> <p><strong>Q1:</strong> when can split inference reduce total gross energy? <strong>Q2:</strong> how does interconnect bandwidth move that crossover? <strong>Q3:</strong> what is the energy–latency trade? <strong>Q4:</strong> what fixed-plus-marginal model describes each target? <strong>Q5:</strong> where do efficiency rankings flip? <strong>Q6:</strong> how sensitive are conclusions to the measurement boundary?</p> </div> <div class="readme-actions"><a <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-18-claude-codex-pet-observer.md</code></p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/run_reports/2026-07-18-claude-codex-pet-observer.md · commit 006eb47"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>run_reports/<wbr>2026-07-18-claude-codex-pet-observer.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 006eb47</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Claude Code → native Codex pet bridge</h1> <p>Date: 2026-07-18<br>Lane: <code>[AGENT]</code><br>Task: <code>CODEX-BRIDGE-PET</code></p> <h2 id="outcome">Outcome</h2> <p>Claude Code&#39;s actual audited fallback, <code>scripts/codex-bridge</code>, can now run its real Sol turn inside a dedicated Codex desktop task. The native pet therefore sees the same running local conversation as the app UI instead of relying on a parallel marker file.</p> <p>The change does not alter routing policy: the model remains <code>gpt-5.6-sol</code>, <code>high</code> remains the safe fallback and ordinary-task default, <code>xhigh</code> remains trigger-only for hard individual work, and <code>ultra</code> remains reserved for Sol sessions that must spawn subagents.</p> <h2 id="corrected-root-cause">Corrected root cause</h2> <p>Recent <code>.codex-bridge/invocation_manifest.jsonl</code> rows and a live Claude review showed that Claude Code was invoking <code>scripts/codex-bridge</code>, which launched standalone <code>codex exec</code> processes. Those processes were real and consumed plan usage, but the Codex desktop pet did not react.</p> <p>The first attempted diagnosis treated <code>~/.codex/claude-spawned/index.jsonl</code> as the pet&#39;s input. Inspection of the installed Codex desktop app disproved that assumption: the pet derives its running state from app-server-owned local conversations. Neither standalone <code>codex exec</code> nor the project MCP server becomes a running conversation in the desktop app merely by writing observer events.</p> <p>The Codex desktop app does expose a user-owned IPC router and a versioned thread-follower operation. A follower turn runs on an app-owned conversation, which gives the pet genuine state and keeps the result available to the script caller.</p> <h2 id="implementation">Implementation</h2> <ul> <li>Added <code>scripts/codex-app-bridge.mjs</code>, a narrow desktop thread-follower client. It uses the configured app-owned bridge thread, passes the selected model, effort, cwd, approvals, and read-only/workspace-write sandbox to the turn, and captures <code>task_complete.last_agent_message</code> from the app-owned rollout.</li> <li>Updated <code>scripts/codex-bridge</code> so <code>new</code> and <code>review</code> use that native route when the ignored local <code>.codex-bridge/app-host-thread-id</code> exists. Machines without that local bootstrap retain the standalone CLI route; <code>CODEX_APP_BRIDGE=off</code> selects it explicitly.</li> <li>App turns are serialized with an ownership lock. Wrapper termination sends <code>thread-follower-interrupt-turn</code>, preventing the app conversation and pet from remaining falsely busy.</li> <li>The existing <code>.codex-bridge/</code> prompt, response, log, status, manifest, and observer artifacts remain intact. Manifest rows now distinguish <code>desktop-thread-follower</code> from <code>cli-bridge</code>.</li> <li>Removed the provisional MCP observer proxy after confirming that its JSONL events could not drive the native pet. Documentation now separates external diagnostics from the pet&#39;s app-conversation state.</li> </ul> <p>The local bridge host created during this run is Codex app thread <code>019f77a6-3612-7332-9f5e-be9fbde56be5</code>. Its id is machine-local runtime state, not a tracked repository setting. After a Codex desktop restart, open the &quot;Bootstrap Claude bridge host&quot; task once if the app has not restored it; the bridge fails with that explicit recovery instruction instead of silently falling back to an invisible standalone process.</p> <h2 id="live-proof">Live proof</h2> <p>The real wrapper command ran a read-only <code>gpt-5.6-sol</code> turn at <code>high</code> effort through the desktop route. The helper reported:</p> <ul> <li>app thread: <code>019f77a6-3612-7332-9f5e-be9fbde56be5</code></li> <li>turn: <code>019f77a9-2827-7de1-accf-ac2eda21927e</code></li> <li>final token: <code>JOULEWISE_NATIVE_PET_BRIDGE_OK</code></li> <li>manifest transport: <code>desktop-thread-follower</code></li> <li>result: <code>OK</code></li> </ul> <p>The Codex app&#39;s own thread reader independently returned that turn as <code>completed</code>, including its commentary, final bridge envelope, and eight-second read-only smoke command. This proves that the script&#39;s actual Sol work was an app-owned local conversation—the state the pet consumes.</p> <h2 id="verification">Verification</h2> <ul> <li><code>python3 -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest tests.test_codex_app_bridge</code> — 2 tests, OK with normal user-level Unix-socket access. Covers the exact desktop request fields, answer capture, termination interrupt, and lock cleanup. The restricted test sandbox cannot bind Unix sockets, so these tests skip there rather than producing a false failure.</li> <li><code>python3 -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest tests.test_codex_bridge_observer</code> — 3 tests, OK.</li> <li><code>bash -n scripts/codex-bridge</code> — OK.</li> <li><code>node --check scripts/codex-app-bridge.mjs</code> — OK.</li> <li>Live native route smoke described above — OK.</li> <li><code>scripts/check-codex-mcp.mjs</code> — all installed-runtime checks PASS with Codex CLI 0.144.0, Claude Code 2.1.214, and Node.js 23.7.0. The restricted first attempt could not write Codex&#39;s user state DB; the normal user-level rerun passed.</li> <li><code>python3 scripts/gen_state.py --check</code> — OK.</li> <li><code>git diff --check</code> — OK.</li> <li><code>python3 -m unittest discover -s tests</code> — 1,722 tests in 378.294s, OK (15 skipped, including the two restricted-sandbox Unix-socket fixtures that passed in the focused user-level run).</li> </ul> <h2 id="workspace-safety">Workspace safety</h2> <p>The work was implemented on the already-dirty <code>impl/env-guard-cooldown</code> branch. Path-disjoint environment-guard implementation, tests, generated site pages, and untracked <code>node_modules/</code> were preserved. No quiet-machine measurement, commit, push, merge, or deployment was performed.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/run_reports/2026-07-18-claude-codex-pet-observer.md · commit 006eb47 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-moe-routing-energy.md:5162:./docs/site/project_status_full.html:9:</code></pre> <p>Key elements:</p> <ul> <li><p><strong>Single controller, flexible transports.</strong> <code>local</code> for one-machine runs; <code>ssh</code> for remote NVIDIA/Orin targets and split experiments.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Two adapter layers.</strong> Runtime adapters answer how a model workload executes; telemetry adapters answer how power and thermal state are measured. They are independent, so any runtime can pair with any telemetry source.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>A target is a composition</strong> of transport + runtime + telemetry:</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Target</th> <th>Transport</th> <th>Runtime</th> <th>Telemetry</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>macbook_m3_max</td> <td>local</td> <td>mlx</td> <td>powermetrics</td> </tr> <tr> <td>nvidia_3050</td> <td>ssh</td> <td>vllm (llama.cpp-CUDA fallback)</td> <td>nvidia-smi</td> </tr> <tr> <td>orin_nano</td> <td>ssh</td> <td>tbd</td> <td>board rails (INA3221)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>pi5_hailo</td> <td>ssh</td> <td>hailo - unsupported (verdict 2026-06-12)</td> <td>wall meter</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> </li> <li><p><strong>Every run writes a self-contained run bundle</strong>: normalized config, device/environment metadata, timestamped event log (lifecycle + phase + token events), raw power trace, backend-native raw telemetry preserved verbatim, logs, model outputs, and reduced summary metrics. Summary numbers are always derived, re-derivable artifacts; the raw bundle is the source of truth.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Typed schemas</strong> (Python dataclasses, standard library only in the core) validate configs and outputs and emit JSON Schema documentation.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Unsupported is a result, not a crash.</strong> Infeasible hardware/model/runtime combinations return structured failure codes (<code>did_not_fit</code>, <code>runtime_unavailable</code>, <code>telemetry_unavailable</code>, ...) and still produce complete bundles - hardware applicability is itself reportable data (this is how a negative Hailo verdict stays a finding).</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Dashboard v1 is a read-only run browser</strong>, generated as static HTML from bundles (run table, per-run pages, power traces with phase shading). It has no orchestration role.</p> </li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-methodology-highlights">Measurement Methodology Highlights</h2> <p>Unless a figure explicitly states otherwise, JouleWise uses gross measured energy within the named measurement boundary as the headline basis. Gross energy retains the idle, model-residency, and runtime overhead present during the measured interval, so comparisons across devices, configurations, and split versus monolithic execution use gross energy. Idle-subtracted energy is reported separately as a within-device secondary view of activity above the measured idle baseline; it is not used to rank devices or configurations. In Q4, the fixed term is estimated from the gross-energy workload sweep and is not set equal to measured idle energy.</p> <p>This reporting choice follows Dr. Rivoire&#39;s advisor review, as recorded in D-067: subtracting idle penalizes energy-proportional devices and rewards high-idle ones; for split runs, subtracting both nodes&#39; idles deletes exactly the cost that the Q1 crossover question adjudicates.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Dual-basis capture.</strong> Every eligible measured request records gross and idle-subtracted energy plus idle variance; the reporting rule above changes no stored evidence (D-067).</li> <li><strong>Measurement boundaries are named, not assumed.</strong> Each telemetry backend measures a different physical boundary - powermetrics: Apple SoC subsystems (CPU+GPU+ANE); nvidia-smi: GPU board only; Jetson rails: module input; wall meter: full system AC. Within-target comparisons are the primary claim type; cross-target comparisons always state the boundary difference, calibrated against the wall meter where available.</li> <li><strong>Uncertainty is quantified.</strong> Headline comparisons use n&gt;=5 repetitions with mean, standard deviation, and 95% t-intervals; outliers are flagged (never silently dropped); raw points appear in every figure. Differences are claimed only from the confidence interval of the predeclared paired/block difference or named model contrast — never from marginal-interval separation — with the D-053 three-way wording rule (below-floor: not resolvable; above-floor non-directional: unresolved; equivalence only via a predeclared gate). Thermal state is controlled with an idle-power-recovery gate between repetitions.</li> <li><strong>Multi-node clock discipline.</strong> For split runs, per-node clock offset is bounded with controller-mediated marker events and recorded; cross-node intervals shorter than the bound are flagged rather than trusted.</li> <li><strong>Measurement quality is first-class data</strong>: requested vs observed sampling rate, dropped samples, idle variance, thermal drift, telemetry source - all in every summary.</li> </ul> <h2 id="experiment-plan">Experiment Plan</h2> <p><strong>Homogeneous baselines (Phase 2).</strong> Per target and model: a workload matrix spanning prefill-heavy, decode-heavy, and balanced profiles (prompt 128-4096 tokens x decode 64-512), n=5, producing energy/token and energy/request with intervals - and reproducing the qualitative prefill/decode power asymmetry that motivates disaggregation.</p> <p><strong>Disaggregation (Phase 3), feasibility-first.</strong> KV-cache portability is the project&#39;s central technical risk, so the phase is a ladder where each rung is publishable even if the next fails:</p> <ol> <li><em>Synthetic transfer microbenchmark</em> (guaranteed): move KV-sized payloads between nodes with both-end power sampling - transfer energy and time vs payload size vs link speed, independent of any LLM runtime&#39;s cooperation.</li> <li><em>Offline replay</em> (primary): persist the prompt cache on the prefill node, transfer the file, resume decode on the decode node - same pinned runtime on both ends. Per-runtime feasibility spikes (mlx-lm, llama.cpp including cross-machine portability, vLLM time-boxed) run before any borrowed-hardware scheduling.</li> <li><em>Live split</em> (stretch): streamed KV during the run; explicitly droppable without harming the study.</li> </ol> <p>Payload sizes are analytically predictable (2 x layers x kv_heads x head_dim x 2 bytes per token, fp16), which drives experiment design - for a 2048-token prompt: a 1.5B-class model ~56 MiB (~0.5 s at 1GbE), an 8B-class model ~256 MiB (~2.3 s at 1GbE). At 1GbE, mid-size-model transfer time is the same order as prefill time on weaker devices - exactly the regime where an energy crossover can exist; the sweep spans prompt lengths and link speeds accordingly.</p> <p><strong>Analysis (Phase 4).</strong> Aggregation over validated bundles with an exclusion log (no silent data drops); a deterministic figure pipeline (every report figure regenerates from a script); a claims-to-evidence index (every quantitative claim traces to figure -&gt; script -&gt; raw bundles); a sensitivity audit checking that headline effects exceed their confidence intervals.</p> <h2 id="phase-plan-detail">Phase Plan Detail</h2> <p>Each phase has a step-by-step plan and an evidence-gated exit checklist in the repository; a phase closes only when every required item has recorded evidence or a documented blocker.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Phase 1</strong> - <code>docs/phase_1/</code>: lock contracts and methodology (done); gather feasibility evidence: advisor scope, Mac telemetry permissions, wall-meter decision, network topology for the sweep, Hailo verdict, NVIDIA/Orin access, calendar mapping.</li> <li><strong>Phase 2</strong> - <code>docs/phase_2/</code>: bundle writer -&gt; mock adapters -&gt; controller -&gt; reducer -&gt; one-command run (all hardware-independent, exact-arithmetic tests) -&gt; then the real Mac slice (MLX + powermetrics, repeated with variance) -&gt; remote targets as access permits -&gt; homogeneous baselines.</li> <li><strong>Phase 3</strong> - <code>docs/phase_3/</code>: feasibility spikes -&gt; split-run config schema -&gt; transfer microbenchmark -&gt; offline-replay splits with per-stage energy decomposition (prefill / transfer / deserialize / decode) -&gt; interconnect sweep -&gt; crossover dataset.</li> <li><strong>Phase 4</strong> - <code>docs/phase_4/</code>: statistics ratification, aggregation, figures F1-F12 (baselines, traces, phase asymmetry, split decomposition, crossover curves, Pareto frontier, interconnect costs, measurement quality), claims index, results + limitations draft, background / related-work draft (new stage 4.6 — the report&#39;s background chapter now has an owner).</li> <li><strong>Phase 5</strong> - <code>docs/phase_5/</code>: verified README quickstart, backend extension guide (verified by a shipped tutorial adapter), sample bundles, dataset freeze with hash manifest and release tag, colloquium slides, final report.</li> </ul> <h2 id="evolution-from-the-original-architecture-sketch">Evolution From The Original Architecture Sketch</h2> <p>The project began from the &quot;Energy Benchmark Architecture And Expanded Plan&quot; sketch. Its architecture survives intact; implementation thinking has been refined in documented ways (full rationale in <code>docs/decision_log.md</code>):</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Original sketch</th> <th>Current position</th> <th>Why</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>Configs YAML/JSON; bundle stores <code>config.yaml</code></td> <td>JSON now; bundle stores normalized <code>config.json</code>; YAML deferred until authoring pain is real</td> <td>zero-dependency core; sorted-key JSON gives stable config hashing for aggregation (D-001, D-007)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>&quot;Likely Python + Pydantic&quot; schemas</td> <td>stdlib dataclasses with the same contract; Pydantic port possible later</td> <td>Phase 1 runs with no installs; semantics unchanged (D-009)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Mac MLX slice implemented first</td> <td>mock vertical slice first, Mac immediately after</td> <td>the harness is proven with exact-arithmetic tests before real telemetry can confound it; Mac remains the first real backend (Phase 2 plan)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Dashboard file-backed; &quot;DuckDB/SQLite if browsing gets slow&quot;</td> <td>static HTML generator; analysis aggregation via CSV + pandas in Phase 4; no DB planned</td> <td>smallest sustainable tool that serves the two real uses: sanity-checking runs and showing progress (D-006)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Offline KV replay before live disaggregation</td> <td>same, hardened into a three-rung feasibility ladder with per-runtime spikes and a same-runtime rule</td> <td>KV tensors are not portable across engines; cross-runtime transfer (e.g. vLLM-prefill -&gt; MLX-decode) is out of scope; heterogeneous <em>hardware</em> pairs use a portable runtime where its backends allow, pending an explicit portability spike (D-015)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>GPU-to-Apple split experiments listed directly</td> <td>pairings are planned only after spike verdicts; synthetic transfer sweep guarantees the crossover dataset either way</td> <td>converts the project&#39;s largest feasibility risk into a bounded one (R-004, R-005)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>(not covered)</td> <td>measurement boundaries, multi-node clock discipline, controller co-residency mitigation, statistical protocol</td> <td>added rigor required for defensible cross-device energy claims (D-003, D-013, D-014, D-018)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Verdict from the 2026-06-09 audit: the sketch remains coherent; nothing in it has been contradicted - the changes above are refinements with recorded rationale, and the repository&#39;s plans are the maintained, authoritative version of it.</p> <h2 id="risks-and-minimum-viable-outcome">Risks And Minimum Viable Outcome</h2> <p>Top risks (full register with triggers and fallbacks in <code>docs/risk_register.md</code>):</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Risk</th> <th>Posture</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>KV persist/resume unsupported in a runtime (esp. vLLM)</td> <td>spikes before hardware scheduling; llama.cpp fallback; synthetic-transfer floor + analytical composition keeps the study publishable</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Cache files not portable across machines/backends</td> <td>explicit cross-machine spike; fallback to same-platform pairs; portability finding is itself reportable</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Schedule vs fixed academic deadlines</td> <td>every phase has a hardware-independent floor; explicit descope ladder</td> </tr> <tr> <td>3080 Ti borrow window slips</td> <td>borrow time is execution-only against a rehearsed runbook; pairing droppable</td> </tr> <tr> <td>No wall meter</td> <td>within-target claims unaffected; cross-target claims carry the stated boundary caveat</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Advisor approval delay</td> <td>all current work is harness-shaped and valuable under any scope</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Minimum viable outcome (worst-case floor; still a complete, defensible capstone if reached): the reusable harness + Mac vertical slice + homogeneous baselines + synthetic interconnect sweep + an analytical split-energy model - honest, measured, reproducible.</p> <h2 id="timeline">Timeline</h2> <p>Dates pending (this is an explicit ask): colloquium date, report deadline, borrow window. Once known they anchor <code>docs/milestones.md</code> and phase target dates are derived backwards (slides want frozen figures &gt;=1 week ahead; the report wants its claims audit &gt;=1 week ahead). Until then, the dependency structure is the schedule: Phase 4 is deskwork and serves as the buffer; hardware-gated steps are scheduled around access windows with desk work filling gaps.</p> <p>Known: the Mac authorization gate closed 2026-07-06 (privileged sample captured, scoped sudo rule installed); remote-device access (NVIDIA, Orin) is the remaining hardware gate. Work paused 2026-06-13 to 2026-07-04 (planned break, recorded in <code>docs/milestones.md</code>).</p> <h2 id="deliverables-at-completion">Deliverables At Completion</h2> <ul> <li>The JouleWise repository: harness, adapters, tests, CI, extension guide, README quickstart that a new user can run in minutes.</li> <li>The dataset: raw run bundles + hash manifest, frozen and tagged, with every figure regenerable by script.</li> <li>The study: where splitting wins, loses, and why - with uncertainty, limitations, and hardware-applicability findings (including negative verdicts).</li> <li>Final report and colloquium presentation, every quantitative claim traceable to raw data.</li> </ul> <h2 id="repository-map-for-verification">Repository Map (for verification)</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Where</th> <th>What</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td><code>README.md</code></td> <td>entry point and quickstart (grows in Phase 5)</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>AGENT_PLAN.md</code></td> <td>phase index and acceptance criteria</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/phase_N/phase_N_plan.md</code> + <code>_exit_checklist.md</code></td> <td>per-phase steps and evidence gates</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/contracts/</code></td> <td>measurement methodology, run-bundle layout, adapter contracts</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></td> <td>every design decision with alternatives considered</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/risk_register.md</code></td> <td>risks, triggers, mitigations, descope ladder</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/milestones.md</code></td> <td>calendar map</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/run_reports/</code></td> <td>dated work logs with commands and outcomes</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>joulewise/</code>, <code>tests/</code></td> <td>the harness package + canonical test suite; the command and CI output own its current result</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="process-note">Process Note</h2> <p>The machinery exists to protect measurement claims from unchecked summaries, stale assumptions, and review-induced drift.</p> <p>This project is developed by a human researcher directing a multi-agent AI system he designed and iteratively engineered over the course of the project — the orchestration itself is a second, deliberate piece of engineering alongside the measurement harness and its benchmark, and by now it is interesting in its own right.</p> <p>The full description lives in <code>docs/orchestration.md</code> (the loop, the roles, the artifact system, and how the topology itself evolved under its own review machinery); this section is the summary.</p> <p><strong>The division of labor.</strong> Ed sets the research direction, the methodology standards (the decision log&#39;s non-negotiables: raw-evidence bundles, dual-basis capture with gross-energy headlines, named measurement boundaries, no unauditable claims), the hardware and access decisions, and — the part that is easy to underrate — the <em>process policy</em>: every rule below exists because he observed a failure or an opportunity and issued a standing instruction. The AI staff executes: the designated lead agent is the final reviewer and single point of accountability: decomposition, design adjudication, every final diff gate, live verification, merges, and bookkeeping. Independent implementation and review agents do the volume work against pinned specs, adversarial review lenses, test writing, and fresh-instance test auditing; specialist agents handle bounded sweeps. Cross-model review is load-bearing by design: the attributed catch record shows the models and review layers catching different classes of defect.</p> <p><strong>The machinery, briefly.</strong> Independent tasks run as parallel git worktrees, the lead driving each stream&#39;s implementation/review pipeline directly (a topology that is itself the product of a signed cross-model meta-review, then validated by a full session with zero coordination stalls — the evolution is traced in <code>docs/orchestration.md</code>). Every implementation passes through a layered pipeline: a design argument round (the implementer must argue trade-offs before coding), fresh-instance counterreview lenses with lead-triaged dispositions, a test-amplification round, a writer-never-reviews-its-own-tests audit, the lead&#39;s diff gate, and lead-side live verification on real hardware — the one layer never delegated, because it has repeatedly caught blockers whose own tests were green (the tests encoded the same wrong assumption as the code). Merges add their own gate: a pre-merge oversight pass by fresh reviewers with distinct angles, and a standing <em>final-head rule</em> — any commit landing after the last review round gets one more fresh review before merge (its first application caught a crash path in a &quot;trivial&quot; late fix). After parallel streams merge, a dedicated integration review hunts the cross-stream defects no per-stream review can see (two interaction defects on its first outing, two more on its second). An event-driven review council convenes for contract-bearing work, and — per Ed&#39;s instruction — its <em>deliberations</em> are recorded, not just its verdicts: the council log preserves positions, the reasoning exchanged, who prevailed and why, and overridden dissents, so a future reader (or model) can reconstruct why any decision was made.</p> <p><strong>The paper trail (each claim traceable to its evidence home; the external re-reduction demonstration is still pending).</strong> Each fact has one home: <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> — the binding design decisions (the log is the count authority), most recording alternatives considered and revisit conditions; <code>docs/council_log.md</code> — the deliberation record; <code>docs/stream_logs/</code> — per-stream decision ledgers committed <em>with</em> the code they justify (wrong decisions are superseded in place, never erased); <code>docs/run_reports/</code> — one record per session with verification evidence, a per-review-layer catch table, and a delegation-calibration ledger (outcomes assigned by the lead after the gate, never self-reported; prompt-defects separated from model-defects). The whole loop is self-instrumenting: every review layer&#39;s unique catches are attributed and tallied, and a layer that stops earning its keep is dropped by its own evidence rule (one already has been). Delegation boundaries move on calibration evidence, not intuition. Lessons are folded into the process playbooks the same session they are learned — measurably: one failure mode recurred five times before its fix was distilled, and zero times after. The loop even reviews itself: a meta-review consensus (C-009) redesigned the coordination topology, and the next session (C-010) validated the redesign with a zero-stall run.</p> <p><strong>What one day of this looks like (2026-07-07).</strong> Five implementation streams plus a repo-wide test audit ran concurrently: statistical uncertainty, contamination detection, deep DVFS telemetry, campaign automation, and a KV-cache size model. All five merged the same day; the test suite grew 254 → 369; the layered review recorded thirteen attributed catches including three blockers that no single reviewer would plausibly have found together. One blocker surfaced only when the real CLI was run against code whose own tests were green, because the tests encoded the same wrong assumption as the code.</p> <p><strong>How the scope grew.</strong> The project began as an architecture sketch for &quot;measure LLM inference energy on edge hardware.&quot; Contracts-first engineering turned that into an auditable instrument: typed configs, self-contained evidence bundles, a strict re-reduction validator. The mock vertical slice proved the math without hardware; the Mac slice produced the first real joules; the flagship run put a 122-billion- parameter mixture-of-experts model through the identical harness and yielded the first real cross-model observation: two confounded points that differ in size, architecture, and quantization, with energy/token behavior consistent with the fixed-vs-marginal model while decode power stays nearly flat — the big model costs time, not watts. This week the instrument gained the statistical and forensic machinery above, and a steelmanned, devil&#39;s-advocated research agenda of 31 tiered questions — 16 answerable on the current hardware alone (<code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>). The pattern throughout: capability first, claims only when the instrument can defend them.</p> <p><strong>And the most recent day (2026-07-07/08).</strong> Four checkpointed streams were resumed, completed, and merged in one session: the integrity/ provenance overhaul (all 31 audit-pinned defects fixed; strict validation now re-derives the power trace from raw evidence), the docs package, the KV-cache replay feasibility verdict, and the complete fixture-first NVIDIA stack. The layered review recorded ~30 attributed catches, including two blockers no implementer&#39;s tests could see (a provenance hash that did not prove the actual generation input; a validation-gate bypass via mutable metadata), two pinned wire contracts overturned by review before they could ever touch hardware, and one fabricated-evidence defect caught only at the lead&#39;s diff gate. The suite went 415 → 546 tests with zero expected failures, and the lead never wrote implementation code and never skipped a gate.</p> <p><strong>Where to look.</strong> <code>docs/orchestration.md</code> is the process description. <code>docs/council_log.md</code> is the deliberation record — C-006 is a full orchestration trace of the five-stream day; C-009/C-010 are the topology meta-review and its validation; C-011 is the critique counter-review. <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> holds the binding design decisions with alternatives considered (the log is the count authority). <code>docs/run_reports/</code> narrates each working session, with per-layer catch tables and the delegation-calibration ledger. The executable orchestration playbooks live outside this repository as reusable skills (council, delegation, multi-stream worktrees, adversarial review, and a top-level operation-loop that sequences them), so the machinery survives this project and transfers to the next one.</p> <h2 id="maintenance-of-this-document">Maintenance Of This Document</h2> <p>Updated at phase transitions and whenever advisor-visible state changes (a gate closes, a verdict lands, the schedule moves). Volatile work-selection facts stay in the state kernel, verification results stay in command/CI output, and decision structure stays in the checked decision-log index. A front-facing change also refreshes <code>docs/site/DRIFT.md</code>; Ed alone regenerates and deploys the site (D-068).</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>PROJECT_STATUS.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

Log</h1> <p>This is the canonical record of design decisions for JouleWise. Every decision that binds later work, trades off real alternatives, or would otherwise need to be re-derived by a future agent gets an entry here.</p> <h2 id="how-to-use-this-log">How To Use This Log</h2> <ul> <li>Before implementing anything non-trivial, check whether a decision here already covers it. Do not silently re-decide settled questions.</li> <li>When you make a new decision of this kind during a run, add an entry, link it from the run report, and reference its ID (<code>D-NNN</code>) in the code review or doc that applies it.</li> <li>Statuses: <code>accepted</code> (binding until revisited), <code>open</code> (criteria defined, evidence pending), <code>proposed</code> (recorded, awaiting Ed&#39;s ratification), <code>superseded by D-NNN</code>.</li> <li>Every entry must include Options Considered and Considerations. A decision without recorded alternatives is not auditable.</li> <li>Revisit triggers are part of the contract: when a trigger fires, the decision must be re-examined, not quietly worked around.</li> </ul> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Title</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>D-001</td> <td>Run bundles store normalized <code>config.json</code>, not YAML</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-002</td> <td>Telemetry sampling via subprocess + file, no controller threading</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-003</td> <td>Timestamp and clock-alignment policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-004</td> <td><code>powermetrics</code> privilege workflow</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-005</td> <td>One bundle per repetition, grouped by experiment manifest</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-006</td> <td>Dashboard v1 is a static HTML report generator</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-007</td> <td>YAML config input is deferred</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-008</td> <td>Split runs arrive via schema v0.2 (<code>run_kind</code> + <code>split_plan</code>)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-009</td> <td>Dependency policy: stdlib core, optional extras</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-010</td> <td>Run ID scheme</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-011</td> <td><code>summary_metrics.json</code> is the bundle completion marker</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-012</td> <td>Failure-reason to run-status mapping</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-013</td> <td>Controller-as-DUT mitigation for Mac-local runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-014</td> <td>Statistical protocol for repeated runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-015</td> <td>Split-mechanism priority and same-runtime rule</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-016</td> <td>Benchmark model selection</td> <td>open (provisional small-model pick 2026-07-06;
