device-list review opened</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-072</td> <td>Standing self-merge-with-full-gate authority (gh merges included)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-073">D-073</a></td> <td>D-016 device-list amendment: Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-074">D-074</a></td> <td>Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-075">D-075</a></td> <td>Extension-axis intake: ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-076">D-076</a></td> <td>Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review): measured-first budgets</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-077">D-077</a></td> <td>Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log.html#d-078">D-078</a></td> <td>Soundness gate: no claim-bearing extraction from time-anchor-defective powermetrics corpora</td> <td>accepted; operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the full repair arc (close-out cap explicitly Ed-ratified 2026-07-22; original-text ratification rides PR #79 review)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <hr> <blockquote> <p><strong>Site view:</strong> the complete entry index appears above; the 72 older full entries are omitted from this page for capsule size. The complete log is the repository file <a href="https://github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise/blob/main/docs/decision_log.md"><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></a>.</p> </blockquote> <span id="d-073"></span><h2 id="d-073-d-016-device-list-amendment-mac-3080-ti-primary-fleet-12-gib-cap">D-073: D-016 device-list amendment — Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the D-071 brief, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/brief.md</code>). The primary cross-target fleet is the 128 GB M3 Max Mac and the 3080 Ti (12 GiB) rig; the G10 capacity cap re-floors from 8 GiB to <strong>12 GiB</strong> (3080 Ti class sets the floor). Jetson hardware is retained as OPTIONAL, non-cap-setting replication — the edge/8 GiB cell can be added later as a replication row without re-deciding this. The split study&#39;s two nodes are the Mac and the 3080 Ti rig. Big models remain open via the Mac-only subsystem (D-071 clause 3). Follow-ons ruled by Ed same session: (a) conditional primary-model repin remains open with a WIDENED candidate search under the new cap (Ed: &quot;is there really nothing better than Qwen3-1.7B? Gemma 4B or something?&quot;) — 3-4B-class models now fit comfortably; (b) dense/MoE pair re-search under the 12 GiB cap (OLMo dense arm failed G4 as published — see the OLMo verification record in the same trace directory).</p> <span id="d-074"></span><h2 id="d-074-conditional-qwen3-4b-primary-repin-olmo-1b-conversion-spike-authorized">D-074: Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the 12 GiB model search, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/model-search-12gib.md</code>). (1) Qwen3-4B becomes the D-016 primary CONDITIONALLY: the repin lands only when the evidence gates pass (immutable source/license, MLX-Q4/GGUF-Q4/CUDA artifact receipts, three-runtime generation, G10 at the 12 GiB cap, KV receipts, thinking-mode policy pinned); any gate failure retains Qwen2.5-1.5B. New evidence era on success: manifests + quant ladder regenerate from one frozen source revision; Qwen2.5 results preserved as legacy. Runner-up Qwen3-1.7B; Gemma-3-4B rejected for the gated custom license + multimodal MLX seam. (2) The time-boxed OLMo-1B original-format→MLX conversion spike is authorized; success revives the matched OLMoE pair, failure files the dated negative finding and the pair defers (Option C) without re-litigation. Both execute next session as agent-lane work.</p> <span id="d-075"></span><h2 id="d-075-extension-axis-intake-ranked-fold-in-without-new-thesis-proliferation">D-075: Extension-axis intake — ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted (Ed-directed intake via the 2026-07-17 evaluation)</li> <li>Phase: Phase 2+ research program</li> </ul> <p>Context: Ed directed a six-axis evaluation and ratified the resulting roadmap at <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/roadmap-synthesis.md</code>. D-055 keeps C5 deliberation in the bank and the registry as the canonical live index; D-070 keeps these axes as stress tests of Q4, caps candidate commitments at L2, and reserves commitment authority to Ed. The disposition ledger is <code>docs/stream_logs/2026-07-17-axes-foldin.md</code>.</p> <p>Decision:</p> <ol> <li>Admit C5-2.5c as the primary speculative-decoding Q4 break-even rider, C5-2.5b as its proposal-work secondary, and C5-2.5d as a mandatory contamination control. Preserve C5-2.5a in the deliberative bank as a deferred candidate rider only; it is not a standalone campaign commitment before a prospective cross-mechanism design is affordable. All four retain the evaluation&#39;s exact ceilings and forbidden upgrades, and C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY is binding.</li> <li>Admit C5-2.11 as the on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and attach it to C5-2.4, C5-1.12, and C-023-QUALITY-EQUIV-QUANT. Preserve C5-2.12, C5-2.13, and C5-2.14 only as candidate riders on the existing context/KV-growth, prompt-cache/replay, and Q4/AP-1 homes.</li> <li>Admit one new canonical RQ row, RQ-AXI-HYBRID-PAIR, at an L2 named-pair ceiling. Attach the attention/context-slope and module-attribution refinements to existing rows. Record kernel/backend provenance as amendments to C5-1.8, C5-2.7, and C5-3.3, not new theses.</li> <li>Keep the roadmap&#39;s do-not-fold set out of the canonical row set. Its negative dispositions and all unresolved feasibility questions remain in the stream ledger, including explicit <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> markers. Intake does not convert an unresolved runtime, model-pair, adapter, or device-fit question into a capstone commitment.</li> </ol> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Mint every evaluated suggestion as an independent live question. Rejected: it duplicates existing homes, imports unidentifiable mechanism claims, and violates D-070&#39;s single-Q4-thesis posture.</li> <li>Admit only the top three ranked items. Rejected: the lower-cost controls, riders, and provenance amendments prevent predictable attribution errors without creating independent theses.</li> <li>Apply the roadmap&#39;s ranked fold-in and explicit exclusions. Chosen by Ed.</li> </ol> <p>Considerations: this is research-agenda intake, not campaign scheduling or evidence promotion. Every admitted candidate/rider remains floor-gated, earliest-phase tagged, capped at L2 unless an already-existing parent row&#39;s separate machinery says otherwise, and subject to its named forbidden upgrade. The published corpus remains claim-evidence-flagged; no fixture, runtime feasibility result, or registry entry is live energy evidence. D-070 remains the authority for Ed&#39;s axis commitments and quiet-Mac ordering.</p> <p>Revisit triggers: a relevant <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> feasibility finding lands; a named runtime/pair becomes unsupported; P2-015 floors make a predeclared effect undetectable; or Ed changes the D-070 commitment set. Revisit by amending the owning row and this decision&#39;s ledger, never by silently promoting an excluded candidate.</p> <span id="d-076"></span><h2 id="d-076-site-capacity-right-sizing-aud-wo-039-review-measured-first-budgets">D-076: Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review) — measured-first budgets</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-17/18. Owner: lead under Ed&#39;s &quot;host the brief&quot; directive (the capacity decision event AUD-WO-039 fenced on). Ruling, encoded in tests with PR #76: the 1 MiB Lakebed hard cap is inviolate; the measured-artifact budget is 1,000,000 B (measured mode via the pinned validator, SITE-02 loud-discovery discipline); the 943,718 B conservative-estimate guard remains ONLY as fallback when measured mode is unavailable (estimator overshoot documented ~4.3% on identical input). WO-039 preservation boundary held: no advisor-facing page, navigation, provenance, or deep link trimmed. Current measured artifact 961,210 B. Revisit trigger: measured artifact within 24 KB of the hard cap forces the next right-sizing review before any addition.</p> <span id="d-077"></span><h2 id="d-077-environment-guard-idle-admission-and-cooldown-v2">D-077: Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Phase: 2 / measurement</li> </ul> <p>Context: a Ventura video screensaver compositing on an awake display was identified as a material, repeatable contaminant. The affected windows showed about 50% GPU duty and were already detected by the existing <code>idle_window_suspect</code> thresholds. The campaign preflight, per-run admission, and D-014 cooldown nevertheless lacked one shared environment policy, exact override custody, and a sustained-window implementation. In particular, the old cooldown could release after one 5-second sub-window even though the contract called for a rolling 30-second recovery window.</p> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Treat doctor output as a quietness certificate and continue to rely on operator judgment between members. Rejected: a point-in-time advisory cannot certify the later measured window and cannot enforce fixed-n admission.</li> <li>Change persistent display/screensaver preferences or allow contaminated members to be skipped or waived. Rejected: campaign preparation must not mutate host policy, and outcome-dependent skipping/waiving would break the fixed-n design and conceal the contamination.</li> <li>Use a hash-bound campaign-policy sidecar, an enforcing campaign preflight, per-run idle admission with one evidence-bearing retry, and cooldown v2 with frozen clean-anchor fallback. Chosen.</li> </ol> <p>Decision:</p> <ul> <li>A shared pure evaluator owns environment findings. Doctor consumes it only advisorily. <code>run_campaign.py</code> consumes it enforcingly after taking the campaign lock and before member 1. Critical unknowns fail closed. Load average is recorded as evidence but is never a member-admission gate.</li> <li>The production quiet-Mac policy requires AC power with an externally connected source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Quiet-mode arming is explicit and transient: countdown, <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, then a complete re-probe. Persistent settings are never changed.</li> <li>An environment override must name the exact snapshot and findings digests it acknowledges. It is recorded as an override, never a waiver, and makes every resulting member universally claim-ineligible.</li> <li>Per-run idle admission reuses the validated <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code> threshold. It permits exactly one fully evidenced retry with distinct raw artifacts. Persistent awake-display, screensaver, or unknown critical state aborts immediately. Production aborts after retry; the exploratory-only <code>flag</code> path completes the fixed-n member but stamps the unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> reason on gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims. There is no skip action.</li> <li>Cooldown v2 amends D-014: recovery requires a complete, duration-weighted, sustained 30-second evidence window; the one-sided rule is <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code>, so a below-reference window is recovered. Nominal thermal state is conjunctive. A calibrated absolute ceiling, when configured, is only an additional upper cap. A preceding baseline is reference-eligible only when its idle window is clean, critical environment checks passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. Otherwise the campaign uses one frozen clean anchor (NEG-8 reference start when present, else the first admission-passing baseline), records its provenance, never updates it from later outcomes, and fails closed when no eligible reference or anchor exists. Historical recovered rows are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>The policy owner is a strictly typed, byte-hashed sidecar under <code>configs/campaign_policies/</code>; policy version and SHA-256 are copied into each governed bundle. Campaign execution defaults to the production sidecar. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy non-enforcing behavior. All bundle/config additions are nullable or omission-serialized; legacy normalized config bytes and hashes are unchanged.</li> <li>This amends D-057&#39;s stable claim-reason vocabulary by adding <code>environment_admission_failed</code> and <code>environment_override</code>. Both are universal and unwaivable for gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</li> </ul> <p>Considerations: environment admission is measurement-apparatus integrity, not post-hoc data cleaning. Duration weighting prevents irregular sub-window cadence from manufacturing coverage. Frozen-anchor provenance prevents a contaminated or outcome-selected member from quietly becoming the campaign&#39;s new recovery reference. The doctor remains useful as an early advisor without claiming more than its snapshot can prove.</p> <p>Consequences: campaign and bundle contracts gain policy/preflight/admission provenance, environment snapshots gain nullable display/screensaver/HID fields plus a post-run observation, and D-014&#39;s recovery wording is governed by cooldown v2 for new evidence. This decision is separate from AUD-WO-033, which remains behavior-preserving; D-077 intentionally changes future measurement admission and cooldown behavior and does not reinterpret sealed historical bundles.</p> <p>Revisit when: live quiet-window validation contradicts the defensive <code>pmset -g systemstate</code> display parser; calibrated platform data justifies an absolute ceiling; or a new platform cannot expose an equivalent critical probe without privilege.</p> <p>Fix-round amendment (2026-07-18): review found that summing sub-window durations as the completeness test made small inter-probe gaps reject an otherwise complete wall-clock window. Cooldown v2 now requires both a retained wall-clock span of at least <code>sustained_window_s</code> and captured coverage of at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code>, with <code>coverage_fraction</code> defaulting to 0.8 and recorded in thresholds, trace rows, and release evidence. The same fix round made the existing frozen-reference rule operational for controller repetitions, attached cooldown evidence to each physical repetition (and each AXI entry), froze the first eligible repetition in execution order, re-probed the full governed environment per repetition, and added a guard observation after every idle capture. Environment-preflight early exits now retain a terminal campaign verdict; missing screensaver defaults domains use the macOS 20-minute default; and the two D-077 claim barriers are registered in the canonical reducer vocabulary. These are defect corrections to the accepted policy, not new policy alternatives.</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <a href="decision_log.html">Recent</a> · <strong aria-current="page">Archive 1</strong></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-moe-routing-energy.md:5171:./docs/site/claims_ladder.html:1:<!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="utf-8"> <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> <title>Claims Ladder - JouleWise</title> <script>document.documentElement.classList.add("js-enabled");</script> <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 100 100'><text y='.9em' font-size='90'>⚡</text></svg>"> </head> <body> <header class="site"> <nav class="nav"> <a class="brand" href="index.html"><span class="dot"></span>JOULEWISE</a> <div class="links"> <a href="index.html">Project</a> <a href="research.html">Learn</a> <a href="advisor_brief.html">Advisor Brief</a> <a href="project_status.html">Status</a> <a href="status.html">Live Status</a> <a href="roadmap.html">Roadmap</a> <a href="process.html">Process</a> <a href="record.html">Record</a> <a href="library.html" class="active">Sources</a> <a href="results.html">Measurements</a> </div> </nav> </header> <main> <div class="doc-layout"> <aside class="toc-sidebar"><div class="card-label">Table of contents</div><a href="#global-rules">Global Rules</a> <a href="#ladder">Ladder</a> <a href="#downgrade-examples">Downgrade Examples</a></aside> <div class="doc-wrap doc-source-docs-contracts-claims-ladder-md"> <p class="doc-meta"><a href="library.html">Back to sources</a> · rendered from <code>docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md</code></p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md · commit db150a0"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>claims_ladder.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit db150a0</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Claims Ladder</h1> <p>Status: binding for reader-facing claims from Slice 2M onward. Decision D-037 records adoption. Per-claim IDs and mechanical enforcement arrive with the Phase 4 claims index; until then, authors apply this ladder during review.</p> <p>This contract governs wording in reports, slides, README/status prose, figure captions, and tables that a reader could treat as a result. Dated run reports, stream logs, council logs, and decision logs may preserve historical wording, but later reader-facing summaries must use the current level.</p> <p>The warning-only prose scan mechanically enumerates <code>README.md</code>, <code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code>, <code>docs/report_src/**</code>, the generated Phase-4 claims projection, Markdown tables/captions under analysis and figure artifacts, and present or future <code>slides/</code>, <code>captions/</code>, and <code>tables/</code> publication trees. Historical <code>docs/run_reports/**</code> records and the decision/council/stream logs are deliberately outside that scan. Warning-only exit behavior remains the D-059 policy: these findings require editorial review but are not structural claim-gate failures.</p> <p>The canonical JSONL accepts two authority-distinct row dialects through one fail-closed validator: the single pre-P2-037 legacy L1 row only under its exact hash-pinned identity, and current rows linked to a governed <code>joulewise.claim_verdicts.v1</code> artifact. Rows with unknown authority fields or a mixture of legacy and engine-linked authority fields are invalid. Verdict semantics belong to <code>joulewise.analysis_engine</code>; the claims-index layer adds only linkage, canonical ordering/rendering, relative-path, editorial, and current production-admission checks. <code>two_look_alpha_spending</code> remains outside claims-index production admission until separately ruled in; current admission is deliberately <code>fixed_n</code> only.</p> <h2 id="global-rules">Global Rules</h2> <ul> <li>Strict validation is the entry ticket for evidence. A run bundle that cannot pass the applicable strict checks does not support a result claim.</li> <li>Measurement boundaries follow D-018. Claims must name the boundary label where it matters, for example <code>M3 Max / MLX / powermetrics SoC rails</code>, <code>RTX / vLLM / nvidia-smi board power</code>, or <code>wall_meter AC</code>.</li> <li>Cross-boundary comparisons are descriptive only unless a named calibration bundle exists for the compared boundaries. Calibration bundles include wall meter or USB-C PD evidence that explicitly bridges the boundary.</li> <li>Comparative claims from 2M use the experiment manifest order. Interleaved order is required where model reload and operational constraints permit; if block order is forced, the claim must say so and remain below L2 unless the Phase 4 drift audit clears it.</li> <li>Detection-floor gates follow Phase 4 Stage 4.0 and Stage 4.5. Effects below the floor are reported as <code>not resolvable</code>, not as wins, losses, or no difference.</li> <li>Energy-per-output-token claims require runtime-observed output token counts, the runtime stop reason, and the output policy label. If the denominator comes from config fallback rather than runtime observation, the claim downgrades to L0 capability language.</li> <li>(2026-07-09) Token-denominated metrics and cross-tokenizer comparison language follow <code>docs/contracts/token_normalization.md</code>, including its stack-identity table, across all surfaces this ladder governs.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ladder">Ladder</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Level</th> <th>Allowed Claim Shape</th> <th>Required Evidence</th> <th>Forbidden Language</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>L0 - Capability</td> <td>The harness can execute this path and preserve auditable evidence.</td> <td>One complete bundle; applicable strict validation; raw artifacts present; boundary label recorded. Config-fallback token denominators may appear only here.</td> <td>faster, cheaper, more efficient, scales, crossover, ranking, law, proves</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L1 - Instrument Result</td> <td>On this exact stack, boundary, workload, and output policy, this measured quantity was observed.</td> <td>n &gt;= 3 strict-valid bundles, or a single run only if explicitly labeled smoke/capability; runtime-observed token counts for per-token claims; stop reason and output policy label; no suspect quality flags unless waived in text.</td> <td>general device ranking, model-family law, cross-target winner, active-parameter scaling result</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L2 - Comparative Result</td> <td>Condition A differed from condition B within the same measurement boundary under a named workload and policy.</td> <td>n &gt;= 5 per condition; strict-valid bundles; 2M experiment manifest order recorded and interleaved where permitted; confidence intervals reported; effect clears the Phase 4 detection floor; same boundary label, or a named calibration bundle if boundaries differ.</td> <td>cross-boundary winner without calibration, universal, architecture-wide conclusion, extrapolated crossover</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L3 - Model Fit</td> <td>A fitted fixed/marginal model predicts held-out cells within stated error for the tested matrix.</td> <td>Designed matrix with holdout cells; strict-valid source bundles; runtime-observed token denominators; residual and sensitivity analysis; detection-floor audit for every fitted effect; boundaries and workload policies stated.</td> <td>law, universal scaling, architecture-wide result, causal language beyond the fitted variables</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L4 - Generalized Finding</td> <td>The finding holds across named stacks, units, or calibrated boundaries under stated limits.</td> <td>Independent replication across a second target or second unit; strict-valid bundles; n and order rules satisfied per condition; named calibration bundles for cross-boundary quantitative comparison; replicated runbook; sensitivity audit survives boundary and version changes.</td> <td>unqualified claims outside tested hardware, workloads, runtime versions, policies, or calibration scope</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="downgrade-examples">Downgrade Examples</h2> <ul> <li>Two strict-valid Mac/MLX/powermetrics points that differ in model size, architecture, and quantization are hypothesis-generating for Q4. They are not an active-parameter scaling result.</li> <li>A same-boundary energy/token difference with runtime-observed token counts but fewer than five interleaved repetitions is L1 until the comparative protocol is satisfied.</li> <li>A per-token result using configured output length because runtime token counts were unavailable is L0 capability language, even if the bundle is otherwise strict-valid.</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md · commit db150a0 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

<!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. Dated completion and disposition history remains below; the generated Current Queue region is the sole live work-selection view.</p> <h2 id="completed-queue-items">Completed Queue Items</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Priority</th> <th>Completed</th> <th>Task</th> <th>Evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>CODEX-BRIDGE-PET</td> <td>P4 Polish</td> <td>2026-07-18</td> <td>Make the native Codex pet reflect Claude Code background Sol work without changing adaptive effort routing</td> <td>No phase exit-checklist row exists for this personal bridge UI integration; actual <code>scripts/codex-bridge</code> route traced, app-owned thread follower implemented, live Sol/high app-thread smoke <code>019f77a9-2827-7de1-accf-ac2eda21927e</code>, focused IPC/termination tests, and report <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-18-claude-codex-pet-observer.md</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>P2-015-SMOKE</td> <td>P2 Next Slice</td> <td>2026-07-17</td> <td>Complete the pre-Window-A production-shaped campaign shakedown through doctor, strict validation, reducer 0.4.2, strict revalidation, campaign verdict split, and approved backup; keep extra samplers disabled pending DF-TELEM</td> <td>No matrix row exists in <code>docs/phase_2/phase_2_exit_checklist.md</code> for this precondition; <code>production_uncertainty_v1</code> PASSED on merged main at <code>runs/window_a_shakedown_final</code> (<code>request_eligible: true</code>, reasons <code>[]</code>, strict pre+post reduce passed, backup exit 0), pinned in <code>docs/phase_2/detection_floor.md</code>; Owner: Ed (ruled on the D-071 brief, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/brief.md</code>). The primary cross-target fleet is the 128 GB M3 Max Mac and the 3080 Ti (12 GiB) rig; the G10 capacity cap re-floors from 8 GiB to <strong>12 GiB</strong> (3080 Ti class sets the floor). Jetson hardware is retained as OPTIONAL, non-cap-setting replication — the edge/8 GiB cell can be added later as a replication row without re-deciding this. The split study&#39;s two nodes are the Mac and the 3080 Ti rig. Big models remain open via the Mac-only subsystem (D-071 clause 3). Follow-ons ruled by Ed same session: (a) conditional primary-model repin remains open with a WIDENED candidate search under the new cap (Ed: &quot;is there really nothing better than Qwen3-1.7B? Gemma 4B or something?&quot;) — 3-4B-class models now fit comfortably; (b) dense/MoE pair re-search under the 12 GiB cap (OLMo dense arm failed G4 as published — see the OLMo verification record in the same trace directory).</p> <span id="d-074"></span><h2 id="d-074-conditional-qwen3-4b-primary-repin-olmo-1b-conversion-spike-authorized">D-074: Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the 12 GiB model search, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/model-search-12gib.md</code>). (1) Qwen3-4B becomes the D-016 primary CONDITIONALLY: the repin lands only when the evidence gates pass (immutable source/license, MLX-Q4/GGUF-Q4/CUDA artifact receipts, three-runtime generation, G10 at the 12 GiB cap, KV receipts, thinking-mode policy pinned); any gate failure retains Qwen2.5-1.5B. New evidence era on success: manifests + quant ladder regenerate from one frozen source revision; Qwen2.5 results preserved as legacy. Runner-up Qwen3-1.7B; Gemma-3-4B rejected for the gated custom license + multimodal MLX seam. (2) The time-boxed OLMo-1B original-format→MLX conversion spike is authorized; success revives the matched OLMoE pair, failure files the dated negative finding and the pair defers (Option C) without re-litigation. Both execute next session as agent-lane work.</p> <span id="d-075"></span><h2 id="d-075-extension-axis-intake-ranked-fold-in-without-new-thesis-proliferation">D-075: Extension-axis intake — ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted (Ed-directed intake via the 2026-07-17 evaluation)</li> <li>Phase: Phase 2+ research program</li> </ul> <p>Context: Ed directed a six-axis evaluation and ratified the resulting roadmap at <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/roadmap-synthesis.md</code>. D-055 keeps C5 deliberation in the bank and the registry as the canonical live index; D-070 keeps these axes as stress tests of Q4, caps candidate commitments at L2, and reserves commitment authority to Ed. The disposition ledger is <code>docs/stream_logs/2026-07-17-axes-foldin.md</code>.</p> <p>Decision:</p> <ol> <li>Admit C5-2.5c as the primary speculative-decoding Q4 break-even rider, C5-2.5b as its proposal-work secondary, and C5-2.5d as a mandatory contamination control. Preserve C5-2.5a in the deliberative bank as a deferred candidate rider only; it is not a standalone campaign commitment before a prospective cross-mechanism design is affordable. All four retain the evaluation&#39;s exact ceilings and forbidden upgrades, and C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY is binding.</li> <li>Admit C5-2.11 as the on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and attach it to C5-2.4, C5-1.12, and C-023-QUALITY-EQUIV-QUANT. Preserve C5-2.12, C5-2.13, and C5-2.14 only as candidate riders on the existing context/KV-growth, prompt-cache/replay, and Q4/AP-1 homes.</li> <li>Admit one new canonical RQ row, RQ-AXI-HYBRID-PAIR, at an L2 named-pair ceiling. Attach the attention/context-slope and module-attribution refinements to existing rows. Record kernel/backend provenance as amendments to C5-1.8, C5-2.7, and C5-3.3, not new theses.</li> <li>Keep the roadmap&#39;s do-not-fold set out of the canonical row set. Its negative dispositions and all unresolved feasibility questions remain in the stream ledger, including explicit <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> markers. Intake does not convert an unresolved runtime, model-pair, adapter, or device-fit question into a capstone commitment.</li> </ol> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Mint every evaluated suggestion as an independent live question. Rejected: it duplicates existing homes, imports unidentifiable mechanism claims, and violates D-070&#39;s single-Q4-thesis posture.</li> <li>Admit only the top three ranked items. Rejected: the lower-cost controls, riders, and provenance amendments prevent predictable attribution errors without creating independent theses.</li> <li>Apply the roadmap&#39;s ranked fold-in and explicit exclusions. Chosen by Ed.</li> </ol> <p>Considerations: this is research-agenda intake, not campaign scheduling or evidence promotion. Every admitted candidate/rider remains floor-gated, earliest-phase tagged, capped at L2 unless an already-existing parent row&#39;s separate machinery says otherwise, and subject to its named forbidden upgrade. The published corpus remains claim-evidence-flagged; no fixture, runtime feasibility result, or registry entry is live energy evidence. D-070 remains the authority for Ed&#39;s axis commitments and quiet-Mac ordering.</p> <p>Revisit triggers: a relevant <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> feasibility finding lands; a named runtime/pair becomes unsupported; P2-015 floors make a predeclared effect undetectable; or Ed changes the D-070 commitment set. Revisit by amending the owning row and this decision&#39;s ledger, never by silently promoting an excluded candidate.</p> <span id="d-076"></span><h2 id="d-076-site-capacity-right-sizing-aud-wo-039-review-measured-first-budgets">D-076: Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review) — measured-first budgets</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-17/18. Owner: lead under Ed&#39;s &quot;host the brief&quot; directive (the capacity decision event AUD-WO-039 fenced on). Ruling, encoded in tests with PR #76: the 1 MiB Lakebed hard cap is inviolate; the measured-artifact budget is 1,000,000 B (measured mode via the pinned validator, SITE-02 loud-discovery discipline); the 943,718 B conservative-estimate guard remains ONLY as fallback when measured mode is unavailable (estimator overshoot documented ~4.3% on identical input). WO-039 preservation boundary held: no advisor-facing page, navigation, provenance, or deep link trimmed. Current measured artifact 961,210 B. Revisit trigger: measured artifact within 24 KB of the hard cap forces the next right-sizing review before any addition.</p> <span id="d-077"></span><h2 id="d-077-environment-guard-idle-admission-and-cooldown-v2">D-077: Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Phase: 2 / measurement</li> </ul> <p>Context: a Ventura video screensaver compositing on an awake display was identified as a material, repeatable contaminant. The affected windows showed about 50% GPU duty and were already detected by the existing <code>idle_window_suspect</code> thresholds. The campaign preflight, per-run admission, and D-014 cooldown nevertheless lacked one shared environment policy, exact override custody, and a sustained-window implementation. In particular, the old cooldown could release after one 5-second sub-window even though the contract called for a rolling 30-second recovery window.</p> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Treat doctor output as a quietness certificate and continue to rely on operator judgment between members. Rejected: a point-in-time advisory cannot certify the later measured window and cannot enforce fixed-n admission.</li> <li>Change persistent display/screensaver preferences or allow contaminated members to be skipped or waived. Rejected: campaign preparation must not mutate host policy, and outcome-dependent skipping/waiving would break the fixed-n design and conceal the contamination.</li> <li>Use a hash-bound campaign-policy sidecar, an enforcing campaign preflight, per-run idle admission with one evidence-bearing retry, and cooldown v2 with frozen clean-anchor fallback. Chosen.</li> </ol> <p>Decision:</p> <ul> <li>A shared pure evaluator owns environment findings. Doctor consumes it only advisorily. <code>run_campaign.py</code> consumes it enforcingly after taking the campaign lock and before member 1. Critical unknowns fail closed. Load average is recorded as evidence but is never a member-admission gate.</li> <li>The production quiet-Mac policy requires AC power with an externally connected source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Quiet-mode arming is explicit and transient: countdown, <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, then a complete re-probe. Persistent settings are never changed.</li> <li>An environment override must name the exact snapshot and findings digests it acknowledges. It is recorded as an override, never a waiver, and makes every resulting member universally claim-ineligible.</li> <li>Per-run idle admission reuses the validated <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code> threshold. It permits exactly one fully evidenced retry with distinct raw artifacts. Persistent awake-display, screensaver, or unknown critical state aborts immediately. Production aborts after retry; the exploratory-only <code>flag</code> path completes the fixed-n member but stamps the unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> reason on gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims. There is no skip action.</li> <li>Cooldown v2 amends D-014: recovery requires a complete, duration-weighted, sustained 30-second evidence window; the one-sided rule is <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code>, so a below-reference window is recovered. Nominal thermal state is conjunctive. A calibrated absolute ceiling, when configured, is only an additional upper cap. A preceding baseline is reference-eligible only when its idle window is clean, critical environment checks passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. Otherwise the campaign uses one frozen clean anchor (NEG-8 reference start when present, else the first admission-passing baseline), records its provenance, never updates it from later outcomes, and fails closed when no eligible reference or anchor exists. Historical recovered rows are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>The policy owner is a strictly typed, byte-hashed sidecar under <code>configs/campaign_policies/</code>; policy version and SHA-256 are copied into each governed bundle. Campaign execution defaults to the production sidecar. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy non-enforcing behavior. All bundle/config additions are nullable or omission-serialized; legacy normalized config bytes and hashes are unchanged.</li> <li>This amends D-057&#39;s stable claim-reason vocabulary by adding <code>environment_admission_failed</code> and <code>environment_override</code>. Both are universal and unwaivable for gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</li> </ul> <p>Considerations: environment admission is measurement-apparatus integrity, not post-hoc data cleaning. Duration weighting prevents irregular sub-window cadence from manufacturing coverage. Frozen-anchor provenance prevents a contaminated or outcome-selected member from quietly becoming the campaign&#39;s new recovery reference. The doctor remains useful as an early advisor without claiming more than its snapshot can prove.</p> <p>Consequences: campaign and bundle contracts gain policy/preflight/admission provenance, environment snapshots gain nullable display/screensaver/HID fields plus a post-run observation, and D-014&#39;s recovery wording is governed by cooldown v2 for new evidence. This decision is separate from AUD-WO-033, which remains behavior-preserving; D-077 intentionally changes future measurement admission and cooldown behavior and does not reinterpret sealed historical bundles.</p> <p>Revisit when: live quiet-window validation contradicts the defensive <code>pmset -g systemstate</code> display parser; calibrated platform data justifies an absolute ceiling; or a new platform cannot expose an equivalent critical probe without privilege.</p> <p>Fix-round amendment (2026-07-18): review found that summing sub-window durations as the completeness test made small inter-probe gaps reject an otherwise complete wall-clock window. Cooldown v2 now requires both a retained wall-clock span of at least <code>sustained_window_s</code> and captured coverage of at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code>, with <code>coverage_fraction</code> defaulting to 0.8 and recorded in thresholds, trace rows, and release evidence. The same fix round made the existing frozen-reference rule operational for controller repetitions, attached cooldown evidence to each physical repetition (and each AXI entry), froze the first eligible repetition in execution order, re-probed the full governed environment per repetition, and added a guard observation after every idle capture. Environment-preflight early exits now retain a terminal campaign verdict; missing screensaver defaults domains use the macOS 20-minute default; and the two D-077 claim barriers are registered in the canonical reducer vocabulary. These are defect corrections to the accepted policy, not new policy alternatives.</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <a href="decision_log.html">Recent</a> · <strong aria-current="page">Archive 1</strong></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

<!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. Dated completion and disposition history remains below; the generated Current Queue region is the sole live work-selection view.</p> <h2 id="completed-queue-items">Completed Queue Items</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Priority</th> <th>Completed</th> <th>Task</th> <th>Evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>CODEX-BRIDGE-PET</td> <td>P4 Polish</td> <td>2026-07-18</td> <td>Make the native Codex pet reflect Claude Code background Sol work without changing adaptive effort routing</td> <td>No phase exit-checklist row exists for this personal bridge UI integration; docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-spec-decode-energy.md:6357:./docs/site/research.html:17:</header> <main> <section class="learn-hero"> <div class="kicker">Interactive field guide · programming knowledge assumed · measurement science taught here</div> <p class="readme-eyebrow">From watts to warranted claims.</p> <h1>How do you measure<br>a machine thinking?</h1> <p class="lede">You already know how programs execute. This guide adds the uncomfortable part: deciding which physical signal belongs to the program, how much noise the instrument adds, and what the evidence actually permits you to say.</p> <nav class="chapter-nav" aria-label="Guide chapters"> <a href="#hard">The hard part</a><a href="#units">Watts &amp; joules</a> <a href="#sampling">Sampling</a><a href="#bundles">Bundles</a> <a href="#floor">Detection floors</a><a href="#found">Findings</a> <a href="#next">Next</a> </nav> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>measurement_methodology.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 6d80039</span></span> <span class="source-chip" title="docs/site_src/research.html · commit 05002b1"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>site_src/<wbr>research.html</span><span class="source-commit">commit 05002b1</span></span></div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="hard"> <div class="chapter-number">01</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">Why this is hard</div> <h2>The model does not come with an energy return value.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">A profiler can tell you which function consumed CPU time. Energy is a physical quantity observed through a separate instrument. You have to align two clocks, define a boundary, and decide what else was happening while the model ran.</p> <div class="concept-grid"> <article><span>Boundary</span><h3>Which power?</h3><p>SoC rails omit parts of the whole machine. Wall power includes more than the chip. Neither is automatically wrong; an unlabeled boundary is.</p></article> <article><span>Attribution</span><h3>Which interval?</h3><p>Load the model too late or stop sampling too early and the number answers a different question than the experiment config asked.</p></article> <article><span>Workload</span><h3>Which work?</h3><p>Prompt length, generated tokens, batching, caching, stop behavior, and content can all change the physical execution.</p></article> <article><span>Noise</span><h3>Which difference?</h3><p>Background activity, thermal state, sampling cadence, clock error, and run order can manufacture a small “effect.”</p></article> </div> <aside class="learn-aside"><strong>The measurement-science move:</strong> replace “I got a number” with “I defined a quantity, captured the evidence, bounded what could imitate it, and stated the claim ceiling.”</aside> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="units"> <div class="chapter-number">02</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">Watts, joules, and idle</div> <h2>Power is a rate. Energy is the area.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">A watt is one joule per second. If power changes over time, energy is the integral under the power trace. That identity is a unit definition—not a JouleWise measurement result.</p> <div class="equation-stack"> <div><span>instantaneous power</span><strong>P(t)</strong><small>watts = joules / second</small></div> <div><span>gross measured energy</span><strong>E = ∫ P(t) dt</strong><small>headline basis within the named boundary</small></div> <div><span>idle-subtracted energy</span><strong>E<sub>secondary</sub> = ∫ (P(t) − P<sub>idle</sub>) dt</strong><small>within-device secondary view only</small></div> </div> <p>Idle is not “free energy to erase.” It is an observed baseline under a stated condition. Subtracting it can help describe activity above baseline on one device, but it can distort comparisons: a high-idle device gets a larger subtraction. JouleWise therefore uses <strong>gross energy for every cross-device, cross-configuration, and split-vs-monolithic headline</strong>. Phase energy is gross-only.</p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>measurement_methodology.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 6d80039</span></span></div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="sampling"> <div class="chapter-number">03</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">How powermetrics sampling works</div> <h2>You never see the continuous curve.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede"><code>powermetrics</code> reports discrete samples from named Apple power rails. JouleWise aligns those samples with runtime events and integrates between explicit measured-window boundaries. Move the toy controls below: the underlying program is unchanged, but the estimated area changes when the window or sample pattern changes.</p> <div class="interactive-card" data-trace-lab> <div The interesting part is what strict validation does with it.</p> <div class="bundle-diagram" role="img" aria-label="Run bundle artifacts flow through strict validation to a bounded claim"> <div class="bundle-box"><span>run bundle</span><code>config.json</code><code>metadata.json</code><code>events.jsonl</code><code>raw telemetry</code><code>outputs + logs</code><code>summary metrics</code></div> <div class="bundle-arrow">replay →</div> <div class="bundle-box validator-box"><span>strict validator</span><p>parse raw evidence</p><p>re-derive windows</p><p>recompute energy</p><p>check provenance</p><p>fail on mismatch</p></div> <div class="bundle-arrow">gate →</div> <div class="bundle-box claim-box"><span>claim ceiling</span><p>L0: auditability</p><p>L1: descriptive</p><p>L2+: only after floor, uncertainty, plan, and evidence gates</p></div> </div> <p><strong>Strict-valid does not mean scientifically conclusive.</strong> It means the recorded artifact is internally valid under the strict contract. A bundle can be strict-valid and still carry flags that prevent a comparison claim. That distinction matters in the newest floor data.</p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md · commit db150a0"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>claims_ladder.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit db150a0</span></span></div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="floor"> <div class="chapter-number">05</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">Detection floors</div> <h2>How small is too small to resolve?</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">Repeat the same condition and the measured energy moves anyway. The false-effect guard floor summarizes how large that repeat scatter—or an ABBA comparison artifact—can look. An effect below the applicable floor is <strong>not resolvable</strong>, not proven absent.</p> <div class="interactive-card floor-lab" data-floor-lab> <div class="interactive-head"><div><span class="card-label">Effect-versus-floor gate</span><h3>Try to clear a real verified floor.</h3></div><span class="status-chip">calibration logic</span></div> <label class="floor-select">Choose the applicable gate <select data-floor-select> <option value="0.527197" data-basis="gross request · absolute repeat">Gross mid-request absolute · 0.527197 J</option> <option value="0.909237" data-basis="gross request · comparative ABBA">Gross mid-request comparative · 0.909237 J</option> <option value="0.536632" data-basis="idle-subtracted request · within-device secondary">Idle-subtracted mid-request absolute · 0.536632 J</option> <option value="0.894215" data-basis="idle-subtracted request · within-device secondary comparative">Idle-subtracted mid-request comparative · 0.894215 J</option> <option value="1.738940" data-basis="gross prefill phase · governing gate">Gross prefill phase gate · 1.738940 J</option> <option value="1.026892" data-basis="gross decode phase · governing gate">Gross decode phase gate · 1.026892 J</option> <option value="4.922865" data-basis="gross suite-item · governing gate">Gross suite-item gate · 4.922865 J</option> <option value="24.618735" data-basis="gross suite-level · governing gate">Gross suite-level gate · 24.618735 J</option> </select> </label> <label class="effect-control">Hypothetical observed effect <input data-effect type="range" min="0" max="30" value="0.70" step="0.01"> <output data-effect-out>0.70 J</output> </label> <div class="floor-track" aria-hidden="true"><span data-floor-mark></span><i data-effect-mark></i></div> <div class="floor-verdict" data-floor-verdict aria-live="polite"></div> <p class="interactive-note">Clearing this numeric gate is necessary, not sufficient. It does not clear clock, sampling, uncertainty, contamination, multiplicity, correctness, or pre-registered analysis-plan gates.</p> </div> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/phase_2/detection_floor.md · commit 907ee58"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>phase_2/<wbr>detection_floor.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 907ee58</span></span></div> </div> </section> <section class="learn-chapter" id="found"> <div class="chapter-number">06</div> <div class="chapter-copy"> <div class="kicker">What the project has found so far</div> <h2>Real floors, plus an important warning.</h2> <p class="chapter-lede">The verified Window-A extraction reports the following false-effect guard floors. <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. class="source-file">docs/<wbr>council_log.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. Anything user-facing (push/merge/publish) follows the user&#39;s standing instructions.</p> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Date</th> <th>Topic</th> <th>Outcome</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>C-001</td> <td>2026-07-06</td> <td>Adopt review/counterreview between Claude and Codex (2H precedent)</td> <td>adopted;
