At the Ed-directed pause (stop card checkpoint #4 + amendments) PRs #50–#53 and #56–#58 stood open and lead-gated with the resume order pinned; after resume, the integration tree (<code>c028-integration</code> @ <code>190a0fc</code>, main post-#55 + 7 branches) caught 38 cross-stream failures, the fix round + cross-stream review cleared them, and the full wave merged SHA-guarded (#50, #51, #52, #53, #56, #57, #58 — P2-037 last), with final main verified green and content-identical to the reviewed tree; follow-up PR #59 (from the cross-stream review) is under review and DOC-008 rounds remain in flight. Delegation infrastructure landed on main: adapter, codex-run-v3, usage guard, scope backstop.</p> <p>Closeout amendment (2026-07-11): C-028 is <strong>CLOSED</strong>. PRs #41-#58 are merged; current main&#39;s canonical suite is 1,220 OK (<code>skipped=10</code>) and the corpus gate is 6/6. PR #59 remains open with a 1,224-test green worktree replay (<code>skipped=12</code>), and <code>impl/doc008-kernel</code> is pushed awaiting PR. These open follow-ups do not reopen the card. Every Window-A software gate and P0-003 are satisfied; quiet-machine execution with Ed remains deliberately separate from landed-software status. NVIDIA/Orin protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL pending live evidence.</p> <p>Layer structure: Sol implementation sessions (xhigh; 2 ultra for the p2041-vetted composition and the P2-037 engine) → review lenses (contract + semantics per stream) → severity-tiered refuters (2 per blocker) → independent post-hoc audits (P2-037) → delta re-audits after fix rounds → lead gates (live runs, arithmetic checks, final heads, CI) → cross-stream integration tree before each merge.</p> <p>Unique catches per layer (D-061 evaluation record):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Sol merge review:</strong> caught the lead&#39;s own merge-resolution error — the branch&#39;s updated P2-005 row silently lost by a whole-file <code>--theirs</code> checkout during the #49 conflict resolution; repaired as a proper 3-way merge (<code>13f6c9e</code>). Only layer to catch it.</li> <li><strong>Refuter tier:</strong> narrowed 2 blockers via CONTRADICTORY paired verdicts — P2-041 B1 (contract refuter confirmed, reachability refuter refuted the broad form → landed as the narrowed shared fail-closed cooldown verifier, <code>f2c4701</code>) and P2-037 F1 (design vs repro refuters split the same way → F1 narrowed before the fix round). The disagreement itself was the signal; neither single refuter would have produced the narrowed form.</li> <li><strong>Delta re-audits:</strong> 2 fresh blockers in paths newly reachable only after the fix round (P2-037 delta re-audit: blocker=2/should-fix=3), plus the recurring symlink pattern — cooldown provenance <code>Path.resolve</code> unwrapped against symlink loop/OSError, wrapped fail-closed with a cross-version regression test (<code>5f1f161</code>). Neither finding existed in the pre-fix tree; the re-audit layer is what sees post-fix reachability.</li> <li><strong>Lead gates:</strong> P2-044 F1 cadence arithmetic verified directly (all-intervals population; binding Qwen-r3 values asserted exactly: median 0.1199250625, ratio 1.0581313969 — <code>dc1ab95</code>); live NV-5 localhost gate 3/3 OK closing the open lead gate on #49 (<code>10e0ad2</code>); live doctor run. All three are lead-live-only — no static layer could produce them.</li> <li><strong>Integration tree:</strong> 38 pre-merge cross-stream test failures caught at the combined head, dominated by REPRO-002&#39;s fail-closed environment/inventory checks meeting post-cut fields from sibling streams. Zero of these were visible in any single stream&#39;s green suite.</li> <li><strong>Enforcement layer (scope backstop, live):</strong> 2 bytecode false-positive firings tuned same-day; NEEDS_SCOPE compliant stops ×3 (p2037 fix round, doc008 ×2) — each returning the correct paths where the lead had guessed wrong.</li> </ul> <p>Scope enforcement fired in production: two sessions (p2043-impl, p2044-fixround) exited SCOPE_VIOLATION with work preserved in evidence bundles, not landed; one wrapper crash (lead in-place edit of the installed runner mid-run) was recovered via a lead-authored recovery row rather than a mutated record — both behaviors are now ratified in D-064.</p> <p>Rough spend (from the two manifests + local usage accounting; estimates, not billing truth): 2 ultra sessions ≈ 100M tokens (p2041-vetted composition, P2-037 engine); 53 recorded xhigh invocations (14 v2-manifest + 37 v3-event-stream + 2 transition-era rows) — local 24h accounting shows 50 xhigh sessions ≈ 171M tokens; 2 high (both FAILED rc=1 resume attempts, work recovered in later sessions) ≈ 40M. Fable lead: ~1.8M generation / ~14.8M billed-ish / ~570M cache reads. Two v3 sessions (doc008-r3, pr59-review) still RUNNING at the manifest snapshot.</p> <p>Spend snapshot addendum (2026-07-11 ~20:00Z, <code>codex-usage</code> 24h window, arc-close truth for the table above; estimates, not billing): 59 Sol sessions / 330.6M tokens / ~17.5h session time — xhigh 55 ≈ 190.4M, ultra 2 ≈ 100.3M, high 2 ≈ 40.0M (both FAILED). Composition (measured from raw session records): ~97.4% of Sol input is cached, output ≈ 0.37% of volume. API-list-price equivalent (GPT-5.6-sol $5/$30, cached $0.50; Fable 5 $10/$50, cache reads $1): Sol ≈ $240, Fable ≈ $810 — combined ≈ $1,050 for the recorded arc; upper bound ≈ $2,300 counting all local Codex sessions (includes non-manifest sessions; resume rows may double-count). Note the inversion: Sol is ~180x the token volume but Fable is ~3.4x the cost — cache reads dominate the lead&#39;s footprint. Snapshot convention now standing in the council skill §Recording + instrumentation.</p> <p>Process artifacts adopted this arc (ratified as/alongside D-064):</p> <ul> <li><strong>claude-codex-report/v1</strong> — canonical machine-parsed session report envelope; run_finished rows record parse validity, finding counts, verification counts, scope flags.</li> <li><strong>codex-run-v3</strong> — append-only event-stream manifest (run_started/run_finished/run_consumed), retry-with-resume, lead-authored recovery rows on wrapper failure.</li> <li><strong>WRITE_SCOPE backstop</strong> — post-run diff vs declared scope; exit 77 + evidence bundle on violation; NEEDS_SCOPE prospective-only expansion (AGENTS.md precedence section, <code>9ca89cc</code>).</li> <li><strong>NEEDS_RULING</strong> — any blocking non-delegable decision early-returns a structured question instead of a guess (<code>31b3f5e</code>); usage guard + usage-pressure mode active.</li> <li><strong>Design-consult-by-default</strong> — Ed-prompted global-rule amendment; exercised for P2-044 (HAC/ESS design consult, <code>827df12</code>) before implementation.</li> </ul> <p>Dissents overridden: none unresolved. The P2-041 RED tranche (ultra round deleting P2-038/P2-040 wholesale) was not landed or argued — it was triaged per-file and rebuilt from main under three Ed-approved C rulings (<code>96e10bd</code>, <code>750f7d0</code>).</p> <p>Calibration note (model-version scoping, per C-027): the refuter contradictory-verdict pattern produced correct narrowings twice; the two scope violations and one thin-output ultra warning are the arc&#39;s recorded 5.6-sol failure modes. Sealed A/B remains the gate before any delegation-boundary change.</p> <h2 id="c-031-d-078-p0-instrument-repair-close-out-session-round-8-landing-round-9-final-confirmation-sign-off-2026-07-22">C-031: D-078 P0 instrument-repair close-out session — round-8 landing, round-9 final confirmation, sign-off (2026-07-22)</h2> <p>Shape: lead resumed the paused arc cold from scratchpad pointers; collected the checkpointed Sol round-8 fix wave; §C-028 delta re-audit (3 fresh read-only Sol lenses over a shared packet → 8 xhigh refuter verdicts, blockers 2 refuters with distinct lenses); Sol xhigh round-8b fix wave under enforced WRITE_SCOPE (one NEEDS_SCOPE early-return, lead-ruled, fixture fix applied at the bench); bounded 8b delta re-audit; lead full-suite gates (2081 → 2088 passed, 0 failures); commit <code>040ca3a</code>; round-9 FINAL confirmation (Sol xhigh review genre); CR9-1 adjudicated as registered limitation L1 per the loop-termination doctrine; close-out <code>debc6d2</code>; PR #79 opened for Ed-named merge.</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li>Sol review lenses: A1 (v3 claim-eligibility contract divergence), B1 (ClockStamp physical-sanity gap → understated B_fiducial ~3 µs), C1/C2 (boundary float, OverflowError escape), C3/C4 (test-wiring gaps).</li> <li>Sol xhigh refuters: killed A2/B2 outright (both plausible, both wrong — A2&#39;s &quot;legacy records break&quot; was self-invalid synthetic-only; B2&#39;s stale-vs-invalid relabel would have broken a ratified distinction); narrowed C1 to a registered nit; split on A1 (contract-confirmed, reachability-refuted) — lead synthesis: pre-existing defense-in-depth hardening, not a round-8 regression.</li> <li>Round-9 confirmation: CR9-1 (floor artifacts self-attesting) — the only finding of the round, repro-backed, lead-reproduced at the bench.</li> <li>Lead unique: false-attribution triage of the 8b audit&#39;s two &quot;blockers&quot; (both were the lead&#39;s own authorized bench edits); the L1 adjudication.</li> </ul> <p>Failure modes recorded: (1) upstream cyber-content filter killed 3/8 refuters mid-run on adversarial phrasing (&quot;malformed/tamper/escape&quot;) — rephrasing as data-quality QA of our own instrument recovered all three (route: keep refuter briefs mechanism-neutral); (2) lead bench-edited the worktree while an enforced-scope Sol session ran in it → false SCOPE_VIOLATION attribution + resume-registry loss (rule: no lead edits in a tree with a live enforced-scope session); (3) the known xhigh review-genre null-final-message mode recurred on round 9; the documented bridge-resume recovery worked first try.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: the 8b delta auditor&#39;s should-fix (OverflowError normalization also reaching v1 replay error behavior) was overridden by lead ruling — frozen-replay doctrine protects computed semantics of parsable artifacts, not crash reproduction on impossible inputs; the reducer&#39;s structured-failure contract governs all protocols.</p> <h2 id="c-032-neg-8-estimand-debate-peer-disagreement-adopted-ed-ratification-2026-07-24">C-032: NEG-8 estimand debate — peer disagreement adopted, Ed ratification (2026-07-24)</h2> <p>Ed directed a formal cross-model debate on the clause-10 ruling before ratifying. Shape: lead position paper + explicit license and request to disagree; one xhigh peer round evaluating five design options plus a peer-proposed sixth; lead adjudication; plain-language synthesis to Ed; Ed ratified the amended design with recorded guardrails (decision log clause-10 addendum). Yield: the peer&#39;s structural correction (anomaly screen must not erase drift from the claim budget) was adopted — the second recorded case of invited peer design judgment beating the lead&#39;s ruling. The debate also surfaced one gap neither model had specced (drift-bound freshness horizon — prompted by Ed&#39;s own risk question) and one open science question (a7-vs-a5 prefill floor scatter, 3x). Calibration note: invited-disagreement debate briefs (steelman each option, demand failure modes + examiner view) produced markedly higher design yield than review-shaped prompts; adopt as the default shape for estimand/contract rulings.</p> <h2>C-033: NEG-8 screen+budget audit gauntlet — a new refuter pairing under A/B, four audit rounds, PR #85 (2026-07-24/25)</h2> <p>Shape: the Ed-ratified SCREEN + BUDGET wave (D-078 clause 10) was taken through four adversarial audit rounds (fresh read-only Sol per round; rounds 1–3 xhigh, round 4 high) with per-severity refuter tiers using a NEW pairing under evaluation — <strong>Opus-contract + Sol-execution distinct lenses</strong> (Ed-directed A/B; now the recorded default per the instrument-mix-authority memory). Three Sol fix rounds (xhigh, xhigh + a high alignment pass, high) plus lead bench fixes closed the findings; two lead-owned decision-log addenda were written at the bench between rounds. Commit stack on main(<code>125a48d</code>): <code>b120d07</code> wave → <code>69b65e5</code> addendum 2 → <code>ad75542</code> fix round 1 → <code>315810a</code> addendum 3 → <code>a5a7acf</code> capsule trim → <code>907ee58</code> fix round 2 → <code>dbf6339</code> fix round 3 → <code>19e15d9</code> assertion restore → <code>60b12af</code> capsule pagination → merged <code>c3e2647</code> (PR #85, 56 files, +6012/−439).</p> <p>Layer catches (unique):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Auditor (fresh Sol, per round):</strong> found real mechanisms in every round — round 1: estimand-dispatch downgrade (row shape selects the legacy gross-only evaluator), allowance fail-open (missing allowances silently become no allowance), anchor-gate bypass on the existing-bundle re-verdict path, and the refusal-registry gap (the authoritative registry test actually failed on <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code>); round 2: coordinated-downgrade v2 (strip basis <em>and</em> the whole drift group together) and the mock-label seam (<code>telemetry_source=&quot;mock&quot;</code> defeats both dispatch and the anchor gate); round 3: TypeError on malformed basis values, telemetry-triangle downgrade into the frozen arm at the whole-window barrier, and loss of nonempty positive-path integration coverage; round 4: two omitted assertions in the replacement companion (nonempty affected-contrast set, <code>n == 5</code>). BUT it severity-inflated repeatedly — of 7 blocker-tier claims across rounds 1–2, refuter synthesis sustained 3–4 at tier (round 3 and round 4 produced no blockers at all: three should-fix, then one).</li> <li><strong>Opus-contract refuter (unique):</strong> F2 collapse (the &quot;broken frozen replay&quot; blocker rested on a misreading of the freshness addendum&#39;s scoping — landed as a documented superseded gross-only wire, not a code fix); F6 refutation (condition-level distinctness was already contract-discharged at the consumer boundary); G1 re-price (the full-strip variant is a subclass of registered limitation L1, whose closure is queued as FLOOR-BIND-01, not a fresh blocker); G2 re-price (the ratified non-mock carve-out plus D-030&#39;s strict/raw-evidence binding bound the exposure); blast-radius refutation of the auditor&#39;s proposed G2 fixture fix (strict validation binds backend raw evidence, so the naive fix breaks legitimate fixtures); <strong>A1 terminal-mock-bar gap — the session&#39;s best catch</strong>: an <em>honest</em> mock member could reach claim evidence with all mock-exempted barriers disabled, no attacker required; the NEG-8 sentinel route on round-3 F2 (the one route with no downstream catch); and the F3 fixture-fix refutation (a production-promoted fixture cannot be strict-valid — use a patch idiom instead).</li> <li><strong>Sol-execution refuter (unique):</strong> discovery of the coordinated-downgrade <em>variants</em> (strip the drift group and restore the headline floors and the record validates clean — reproduced on the repo fixture, gate <code>20.799350577898302 → 20.399350577898304</code>, exactly the fixture&#39;s 0.4 J allowance; asymmetric removal from the comparative record alone also validates clean); the G2A adjacent blocker (the reduce layer independently trusts metadata/summary mockness in the environment and CPU-admission barriers, so fresh re-reduction reproduces the forged exemption and strict stored-vs-fresh comparison is not a backstop); identification of the authoritative mockness source (custody-bound <code>config().hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bound through <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>); the <code>mock:*</code> tagged-source class caveat (<code>axi_valid_burst</code> config <code>mock</code> vs summary <code>mock:target</code> — compare backend <em>class</em>, not raw strings); and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); the capsule shard-budget trim (<code>a5a7acf</code>) and the pagination ruling that followed (deterministic <code>D-NNN</code> pagination + D-076 artifact-cap redirects); the battery-flake adjudications; and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Re-priced by refuters before fixing: 4 of those (r1 F4 blocker→should-fix; r2 G1/G2 blocker→should-fix; r1 F2 blocker→docs-only, landed as contract clarification). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

<h1>JouleWise: Project Status, Plan, And Architecture</h1> <p>Audience: project advisor. This is the standalone monitoring document - it summarizes what the project is, how it is built, where it stands, and what it needs, without requiring any other file. Pointers into the repository are provided for anyone who wants the full evidence trail.</p> <ul> <li>Freshness owner: phase completion lives in the phase exit checklists; live gates and work selection live only in the generated state-kernel regions of <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> and <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>; the canonical suite command and CI own the current verification result. This page deliberately does not duplicate volatile commit, pull-request, queue, or test-count facts.</li> <li>Repository state: <code>main</code> contains the repaired measurement instrument (D-078 phase 0) and the audited screening and uncertainty-budget rules (D-078 clause 10; council C-033). The repaired-instrument collection has 229 members across four bracketed windows, a5-a8. Those windows are useful diagnostic evidence that the instrument works, but they are not claim-bearing and do not yet publish a floor. The next step is one clean prospective quiet-machine collection following <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>; if it passes, it will produce the first claim-grade floors before the a8 re-verdict and Splitwise sizing.</li> <li>Project phase: see the phase exit checklists for exact completion state; live eligibility and next work come from the generated state kernel, not this reader-facing summary.</li> <li>Repository: <code>github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</code> (branch <code>main</code>)</li> <li>Live status site: <a href="https://quiet-signal-6af8833395.lakebed.app">https://quiet-signal-6af8833395.lakebed.app</a> (Lakebed capsule; it is an Ed-deployed snapshot, not the repository authority. <code>docs/site/DRIFT.md</code> records known differences; agents refresh that report when front-facing state changes and never regenerate or deploy the site.)</li> </ul> <h2 id="current-repository-view-30-second-read">Current Repository View — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The repaired instrument has completed its first collection era, but the first claim-grade floor is still ahead.</strong> The D-078 phase-0 repair fixed the timing and calibration path on 2026-07-22. Four bracketed windows then collected 229 strict members (a5-a8). They are retained as non-claim-bearing diagnostic, instrument-proving evidence: they showed that the repaired path works and exposed the remaining drift-screen problem, but they are not a published floor set.</p> <p>That problem is now resolved in the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (D-078 clause 10). Gross and idle-subtracted energy are screened separately; each passing window keeps a nonzero drift allowance in its uncertainty budget; the drift bound expires after 24 hours; fallback-clock members cannot support a floor; and mock evidence is identified from the bound configuration and barred from claims. The next quiet session will mint its bound inside the window and collect three start references, one midpoint reference, and three end references. The older 222-bundle floor table below remains visible as a caveated historical record, not the current measurement posture.</p> <p>AXI-SB remains <code>supported</code> for native static-batch runtime feasibility with request-scoped observability; AXI-SC is <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code> on the pinned runtime because the required speculative-decode/MTP observability or execution surface is absent. Neither verdict is an energy result. Remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL, and the generated state kernel remains the work-selection authority.</p> <h3>Published Window-A floor summary</h3> <blockquote> <p><strong>CAVEAT (2026-07-19 soundness audit):</strong> a trace-time-anchor defect was found in the powermetrics evidence path (power timestamps misaligned with runtime events at the ~0.5–1 s scale). It affects the corpora behind this table; every row below is <strong>under re-adjudication</strong> and none should be cited as a promoted floor until the instrument is repaired and the rows re-extracted. Record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>.</p> </blockquote> <p>Every energy value below is a false-effect guard floor in joules on the <strong>Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC-rail boundary (CPU + GPU + ANE)</strong>. Gross is the D-067 headline basis; idle-subtracted values are labeled within-device secondary views. Absolute rows use repeated identical conditions; comparative rows use same-condition ABBA blocks. Each primary row uses <code>n=10</code> strict-valid bundles or ABBA blocks.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>window / basis</th> <th align="right">absolute floor</th> <th align="right">comparative floor</th> <th align="right">computed <code>floor_gate_j</code> / disposition</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>mid request, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.527 J</td> <td align="right">0.909 J</td> <td align="right">0.909 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>mid request, idle-subtracted — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.537 J</td> <td align="right">0.894 J</td> <td align="right">0.894 J; within-device secondary</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short request, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.052 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">absolute floor only</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short request, idle-subtracted — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.059 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">absolute floor only; within-device secondary</td> </tr> <tr> <td>prefill phase, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">1.477 J</td> <td align="right">1.739 J</td> <td align="right">1.739 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>decode phase, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.786 J</td> <td align="right">1.027 J</td> <td align="right">1.027 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short-prefill stress, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.027 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">smoke-only; <code>not_resolvable_sample_count</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>suite item, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.333 J</td> <td align="right">4.923 J</td> <td align="right">4.923 J; drift review required</td> </tr> <tr> <td>suite level, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">1.664 J</td> <td align="right">24.619 J</td> <td align="right">24.619 J; drift review required</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>The start/end NEG-8 reference pair is an <code>n=2</code> drift diagnostic, not a campaign floor. Its gross request energy moved by 7.659 J; the idle-subtracted within-device secondary view moved by 6.608 J (same boundary). Verified extraction: <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-floor-extraction/extraction-verified.json</code>; reader deliverable: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-17-window-a-brief.html</code>.</p> <h3>2026-07-19 re-calibration under the environment guard — PRELIMINARY</h3> <p>The caveated suite rows were re-measured in two bracketed windows under the D-077 guard: <strong>94 strict-valid bundles</strong>, all admission predicates satisfied. Reviewed readout: suite gross <strong>147.96 ± 0.39 J</strong> clean (contaminated cells were ~+30%); frozen-estimator provisional comparative floor <strong>≈ 1.13 J (~0.77%)</strong> from 5 of 10 planned ABBA blocks (~22× tighter, same estimator, than the caveated figure); long-decode <strong>83.9 mJ/output-token</strong>, matching the 07-17 decode cell to ~0.1%. That corpus was claim-ineligible on source provenance (dirty collection tree); details: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-19-recalibration-update.html</code>.</p> <p>UPDATE (2026-07-19 night): the clean re-run is done — 288 strict-valid bundles with clean source provenance (<code>runs_recal3/4/5/6_20260719/</code>) cover every planned Window-A cell except DF-TELEM at planned n, including the complete n=10 suite-ABBA comparative cell; the source provenance gate is closed. <strong>SUPERSEDING UPDATE (2026-07-19/20): a same-day soundness audit found a timing bug, and no energy number from the existing recordings will be used for claims until re-measurement.</strong> In plain terms: the power meter and the workload log time on two different clocks, and our alignment between them could be off by up to ~1 second. Energy is computed by summing meter samples inside the workload&#39;s start/stop window, so a misaligned window integrates the wrong slice of the recording — dramatic for sub-second test runs (one 0.37 s run read 0.27 J when its true consumption, plainly present in the recording, was <del>8 J), and a meaningful hidden uncertainty (</del>±10 J) even on 60-second runs. Nothing measured negative; the recordings are intact and self-consistent; long-run repeatability (~0.3% across nights) shows the platform is stable. Very short workloads are simply below this instrument&#39;s resolution and will not be claimed — by design, not workaround. The fix (align on the meter&#39;s own timestamps, attach an explicit uncertainty range to every number, calibrate end-to-end with 40 precisely-timed GPU bursts before new data) is implemented and in adversarial review. Plain-language explainer: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-20-timing-defect-explainer.md</code>; technical record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>REPAIR COMPLETE (2026-07-22): the instrument repair is finished and signed off.</strong> Over three days the timing defect was fixed and the whole measurement chain was hardened through nine rounds of independent adversarial review (each round tried to break the instrument; the last round found one remaining gap, recorded below). In plain terms, the instrument now: (a) knows precisely when its power readings happened relative to the model&#39;s work (the clock-alignment fix, with the alignment uncertainty — about 27 milliseconds — carried into every result as an explicit error bar); (b) proves its own calibration is genuine and fresh — a calibration recording that was tampered with, mislabeled, taken under the wrong procedure, or older than 24 hours is automatically rejected; and (c) refuses to report a result rather than report a doubtful one, in every failure case we could construct. One known limitation is recorded honestly: the file that stores the detection-floor statistics is not yet cryptographically tied back to the raw measurements it came from, so we only trust such files when our own pipeline produced them in the same verified session (a fix is queued). Live validation on the real hardware passed: the validation recording (made under the earlier 40-pulse calibration procedure) detected all 40 calibration pulses with no false detections, and a test measurement reproduced the expected physics where the old defective pipeline had been wrong by a factor of ~28. Production measurements will use the newer 59-pulse calibration procedure, which supports the stronger statistical guarantee we quote for the timing error bar. Next: a fresh calibration and re-collection of the measurement campaign under the repaired instrument. Record: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-20-p0-instrument-repair.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>COLLECTION ERA UPDATE (2026-07-24): the repaired instrument has now been proven in production.</strong> Over two nights we collected 229 clean measurements across four properly-bracketed windows. The standout result: two identical reference measurements taken three hours apart agreed to within 0.007 joules on a ~38.5 joule task — about 0.02%, which is excellent repeatability for whole-system power measurement. The windows are not yet &quot;claim-grade&quot; for one honest reason: our own stability check (comparing a reference task at each window&#39;s start and end) was found to be asking a mathematically unanswerable question, so it failed every window on a technicality while the underlying data was good. After a formal debate between the two AI models working on the project — which the reviewing model won on one substantive point — the check was redesigned and ratified: windows are now screened for anomalous drift against a limit derived from measured repeatability (instead of an arbitrary constant), and any drift observed is carried into the results&#39; error bars rather than being ignored once a window &quot;passes&quot;. Reference measurements are also being tripled at each window edge. One collection session under the new rules produces the project&#39;s first claim-grade detection-floor table, which then sizes the Splitwise replication experiments. Records: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-23-window-a-collection-arc.md</code>, decision log D-078 clauses 8-10.</p> <p><strong>SCREENING RULES BUILT, AUDITED, AND MERGED (2026-07-25; council C-033).</strong> The redesigned stability screen described above is now implemented and on main: both energy families are screened separately, every passing window carries an explicit drift allowance into its error bars, drift limits expire after 24 hours so stale calibrations cannot be reused, and a measurement whose internal clock had to be guessed can never anchor a result (that one rule alone corrected a floor that was overstated by roughly a factor of three). The code went through an unusually deep adversarial review — four independent audit rounds and three rounds of cross-examination between two different AI models — which caught and fixed several ways the new rules could have been silently bypassed. The step-by-step measurement procedure for the next collection session is written up in <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>. Records: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-24-screen-budget-gauntlet.md</code>, council log C-033.</p> <h3>Exploratory follow-on — not a promoted claim</h3> <p>Nine additional strict-valid, collection-usable bundles cover three repetitions each of unmatched OLMoE-1B-7B BF16, Qwen3-4B INT4, and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4 configurations on the fixed five-item <code>jw_mixed_v1_sentinel</code> shape. Every bundle is claim-evidence-flagged, the model/config points differ in architecture, scale, tokenizer, and quantization, and the repetition count is below the headline protocol. The values are therefore descriptive <strong>EXPLORATORY / L1-legacy observations only</strong>.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>unmatched configuration</th> <th align="right">mean gross suite energy — Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails (CPU + GPU + ANE)</th> <th align="right">mean gross energy/generated output token — same boundary</th> <th align="right">runtime-observed output throughput</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>OLMoE-1B-7B BF16</td> <td align="right">229.028 J (227.141–231.790 J)</td> <td align="right">178.928 mJ/token (177.454–181.086 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">122.361 tok/s (122.261–122.481 tok/s)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3-4B INT4</td> <td align="right">362.772 J (362.642–362.903 J)</td> <td align="right">283.416 mJ/token (283.314–283.518 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">106.519 tok/s (106.470–106.545 tok/s)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4</td> <td align="right">1072.273 J (1061.722–1085.144 J)</td> <td align="right">837.713 mJ/token (829.471–847.769 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">39.473 tok/s (39.349–39.569 tok/s)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Each bundle emitted 1,280 generated output tokens. Gross per-output-token values above are derived from the gross suite numerator; the stored <code>energy_output_token_j</code> field instead uses the idle-subtracted numerator and is retained as a labeled within-device secondary view in the full extraction. For the like-for-like suite-level gross window on the Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC-rail boundary, the exploratory OLMoE-versus-Qwen3-4B mean gap is 133.720 J, above the published 24.619 J suite-level gross <code>floor_gate_j</code>. That only says the descriptive gap exceeds the measurement guard: unmatched configurations, evidence flags, drift review, and the lack of a prospective contrast still prohibit efficiency or architecture claims. Every aggregate and raw repetition is bundle-cited in <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-exploratory-block/results.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-09-c-027-whole-project-council-review-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-09, C-027 whole-project council review) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The project put itself in front of a hostile examiner and corrected its own front page.</strong> A seven-lens cross-model review (new Codex model, extra-high reasoning) plus an independent final examiner audited the docs, the scientific claims, the statistics implementation, the architecture, and the operating loop itself. Verdict: the evidence discipline and instrument core are sound, but reader-facing claims had drifted from the evidence (the 1.5B per-token headline used the wrong denominator — now corrected as <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~79-90 mJ per generated output token), the D-053 contrast-CI machinery exists as binding specs but not yet as code (now owned as queue rows P2-037..P2-042 and gating Window-A interpretation), and the loop&#39;s own audit trail and the capstone-critical path (grading rubric, report skeleton, off-machine backup, one data-to-figure slice) need attention before any new breadth. All measured values above remain legacy L1 preliminary observations. Full adjudicated record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-09-c027-whole-project-review.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-09-advisor-status-cockpit-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-09, advisor status cockpit) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The public preview is being upgraded for live advisor observation.</strong> The project-status page remains generated from repository evidence, but Lakebed now has a narrow fail-soft live overlay contract: freshness from GitHub commit checks plus parsed current fields from <code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code>, <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>, <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>, and the risk register. The advisor cockpit adds live snapshot state, attention items, campaign readiness, evidence cards, and claim-ceiling panels; the Story page drops hand-authored volatile counts. The operational policy is D-051: repo markdown remains the source of truth and Lakebed never hides static provenance. Current work follows <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>: C-019 shakedown, then P2-015 quiet calibration for Window A (the CP-5 stop card was cleared 2026-07-09).</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-08-all-four-streams-merged-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-08, all four streams merged) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>Everything landed.</strong> The multi-stream session merged as four PRs: P2-013 and P2-014 are closed — all 31 audit pins fixed, the suite passed with zero expected failures (current count authority is RUN_STATE.md Current Verification; the suite-build merge was 732 tests and the post-alignment state is 734), bundle provenance now records prompt/workload identities, and <code>validate-bundle --strict</code> includes the powermetrics raw-plist-to-trace gate plus the legacy additive-summary comparison. The six existing real corpus bundles pass strict read-only and unrewritten; strict proves re-derivation of the recorded evidence, not independent rerunning of the hardware session. New-era bundles must carry shape-valid provenance to pass. The Stage 3.0.1 KV spike is merged with a lead-reverified verdict of <code>replay_supported</code> (tokens identical; cache size +0.018% vs prediction) — Phase 3&#39;s central technical risk is retired on current hardware. The fixture-first 2K NVIDIA stack is merged; ALL its protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL until first live hardware contact (the live-verification checklist is ready). The independent project critique now carries a second-pass reassessment (its recommendations that became code are marked resolved; 16/17 of its checkable claims were lead-verified against file evidence): <code>docs/project_critique_review.html</code>. Next: the detection-floor calibration (P2-015) then the 2M two-model baseline campaign on a quiet machine. Reader-facing status below defers to the phase checklist matrix rows for per-item authority.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-2026-07-07-fifth-update-30-second-read">Previous Update (2026-07-07, fifth update) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The instrument grew four capabilities in one session and is now campaign-ready.</strong> <em>(Historical claim; C-027 (2026-07-09) supersedes the gating: execution is conditioned on P0-003 backup, P2-038, P2-039, and P2-015-SMOKE.)</em> Five parallel work streams landed (PRs #2-#6): (1) <strong>statistical uncertainty</strong> — every multi-repetition experiment now carries per-metric 95% confidence intervals with outlier detection and explicit below-protocol flags, re-derivable byte-identically from the raw evidence bundles (verified on a live 3-repetition run as <strong>D-014 verification workload, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> 99.19 ± 1.36 mJ/output-token); (2) <strong>contamination detection</strong> — an idle-window quality gate that mechanically flags runs taken on a non-quiet machine (it caught its first real contamination during verification); (3) <strong>deep telemetry</strong> — per-sample GPU/CPU-cluster frequency and residency forensics plus a machine-state snapshot in every bundle; (4) <strong>campaign automation</strong> — a deterministic config-matrix generator and a resumable sequential runner, so the planned two-model baseline matrix (4 workload shapes × 2 models × 5 repetitions) runs unattended. A review council also produced a hardware-tiered research agenda: 16 questions answerable on current hardware alone, 10 more behind planned gates (<code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>). The P2-013 evidence-integrity and P2-014 provenance fixes are now complete; next Mac corpus step is the baseline matrix on a quiet machine.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-2026-07-07-fourth-update-30-second-read">Previous Update (2026-07-07, fourth update) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>A flagship-class model is now benchmarked.</strong> Qwen3.5-122B (Feb 2026 generation, 122B-parameter mixture-of-experts with 10B active, a reasoning model) ran through the identical harness and workload on the M3 Max. <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~304.0 J per 512-token request. <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~298.7 J per request and ~583 mJ per generated output token. Throughput was 46 tokens/s, and the gross-energy sample CV was 0.3% across three sequential repetitions in one warm-cache session. The earlier model recorded <strong>P2-003, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~47.2 J per request and <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~87 mJ per generated output token at 257 tok/s. <em>(Metric bases and CV wording corrected 2026-07-09, C-027.)</em> First cross-model finding: the two measured points differ in size, architecture, and quantization, so they are not a demonstrated scaling law. They are, however, consistent with the fixed-vs-marginal structure Q4 models: <strong>unsubtracted decode-window mean power — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~23.5 W for P2-003 and ~27.5 W for FLAGSHIP-001, while the bigger model&#39;s cost showed up mostly as time. Also this update: the research agenda grew to six named questions (Q4-Q6) after a multi-model review council, with a curated question bank (<code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>) and an instrument roadmap (richer telemetry parsing, a difficulty-graded scored workload suite, and implementing the statistical-uncertainty protocol) queued.</p> <h2 id="update-ledger">Update Ledger</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>date</th> <th>label</th> <th>one-line outcome</th> <th>run-report link</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>2026-07-19</td> <td>Measurement-soundness audit (Ed-directed)</td> <td>VERDICT: unsound for claim-bearing use as recorded — trace-time-anchor defect misattributes request/phase energies (all four P0s lead-verified); metric-level prechecks already failed 238/288 request metrics; four cooldown cap hits unjoined; analysis-engine wire incompat. Corpora demoted to instrument evidence; published 07-17 floor table caveated; instrument-repair path defined.</td> <td><code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>2026-07-19</td> <td>Extended clean-provenance re-collection</td> <td>266/266 strict-valid bundles with clean SOURCE provenance from clean main (288 total with the completion window); all planned cells except DF-TELEM executed at planned n; one unlock abort quarantined (guard&#39;s 4th live catch); Sol recompute audit PASS on arithmetic. See the superseding soundness-audit row above for claim status.</td> <td><code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-19-recal456-extended-window.md</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>2026-07-19</td> <td>Suite re-calibration under the guard (preliminary, review-corrected)</td> <td>94 strict-valid bundles; suite 147.96 ± 0.39 J clean; provisional comparative floor ≈ 1.13 J (~0.77%, 5/10 blocks); claim-ineligible on provenance pending clean re-run; three-lens review corrected two over-promoted claims.</td> <td><code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-19-d077-recal-window.md</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>2026-07-18</td> <td>Contamination diagnosis + environment-guard hardening (D-077)</td> <td>Suite-cell inflation attributed to the macOS video screensaver on an awake idle display (43/50 bundles; power-source hypothesis refuted); suite comparative cells caveated pending re-run; the D-077 guard (preflight, idle admission, cooldown v2, claim barrier, anchor custody) was built and taken through an eight-round adversarial arc.</td> <td><code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-17-environment-guard.md</code>; class="source-file">docs/<wbr>council_log.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Council Log</h1> <p>Chronicle of multi-model review councils: sessions where more than one model reviews, counterreviews, or votes on JouleWise work before it lands. Companion to <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> (which records WHAT was decided about the system; this file records HOW cross-model review reached it). One entry per council session; keep entries concise — positions, votes, resolutions, and follow-ups, not transcripts.</p> <p>Standing council roles (adopted C-001; process decision D-031):</p> <ul> <li><strong>Claude (lead/orchestrator)</strong> — scopes work, diagnoses live/hardware failures, runs adversarial review workflows, owns bookkeeping and the final merge decision, and is the only member that touches real hardware.</li> <li><strong>Codex / gpt-5.5 (peer implementer-reviewer)</strong> — implements against pinned specs, counterreviews findings on its own code, reverse-reviews Claude&#39;s commits and orchestration decisions, and is asked for design judgment explicitly (&quot;argue the tradeoffs before you code&quot;).</li> <li><strong>Opus subagents (fast reviewers)</strong> — parallel lower-level sweeps (commit hygiene, docs consistency, fixture audits) whose findings feed the discussion; cheap enough to run every session.</li> </ul> <p>(Amended 2026-07-08: the Opus fast-reviewer tier was dropped at C-006 after zero unique catches; lead-driven pipelines are the default per C-010; Ed granted standing self-merge-with-review authority in the C-010 addendum.)</p> <p>Disagreements are discussed in at most one or two rounds; unresolved disagreements are decided by the lead and recorded here with the dissent. Anything user-facing (push/merge/publish) follows the user&#39;s standing instructions.</p> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Date</th> <th>Topic</th> <th>Outcome</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>C-001</td> <td>2026-07-06</td> <td>Adopt review/counterreview between Claude and Codex (2H precedent)</td> <td>adopted; Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Re-priced by refuters before fixing: 4 of those (r1 F4 blocker→should-fix; r2 G1/G2 blocker→should-fix; r1 F2 blocker→docs-only, landed as contract clarification). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

Do not silently re-decide settled questions.</li> <li>When you make a new decision of this kind during a run, add an entry, link it from the run report, and reference its ID (<code>D-NNN</code>) in the code review or doc that applies it.</li> <li>Statuses: <code>accepted</code> (binding until revisited), <code>open</code> (criteria defined, evidence pending), <code>proposed</code> (recorded, awaiting Ed&#39;s ratification), <code>superseded by D-NNN</code>.</li> <li>Every entry must include Options Considered and Considerations. A decision without recorded alternatives is not auditable.</li> <li>Revisit triggers are part of the contract: when a trigger fires, the decision must be re-examined, not quietly worked around.</li> </ul> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Title</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>D-001</td> <td>Run bundles store normalized <code>config.json</code>, not YAML</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-002</td> <td>Telemetry sampling via subprocess + file, no controller threading</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-003</td> <td>Timestamp and clock-alignment policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-004</td> <td><code>powermetrics</code> privilege workflow</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-005</td> <td>One bundle per repetition, grouped by experiment manifest</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-006</td> <td>Dashboard v1 is a static HTML report generator</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-007</td> <td>YAML config input is deferred</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-008</td> <td>Split runs arrive via schema v0.2 (<code>run_kind</code> + <code>split_plan</code>)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-009</td> <td>Dependency policy: stdlib core, optional extras</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-010</td> <td>Run ID scheme</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-011</td> <td><code>summary_metrics.json</code> is the bundle completion marker</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-012</td> <td>Failure-reason to run-status mapping</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-013</td> <td>Controller-as-DUT mitigation for Mac-local runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-014</td> <td>Statistical protocol for repeated runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-015</td> <td>Split-mechanism priority and same-runtime rule</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-016</td> <td>Benchmark model selection</td> <td>open (provisional small-model pick 2026-07-06;
